तव राज्यस्य संप्राप्तिर्यथा भूयोऽपि जायते .. 42 ..
5.208.m: Listen, O King, I shall explain how purification will come about, / and how the regain of your kingdom will take place again.

5.208.s:
tava bhūmau mahāpuṇyamasti kṣetraṃ jagattraye ..
hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñaṃ tu tīrthaṃ tatrāsti śobhanam ..
śaṃkhatīrthamiti khyātaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam.. 43..
5.208.d:
तव भूमौ महापुण्यमस्ति क्षेत्रं जगत्त्रये ..
हाटकेश्वरसंज्ञं तु तीर्थं तत्रास्ति शोभनम् ..
शंखतीर्थमिति ख्यातं सर्वपातकनाशनम्.. 43..
5.208.m: In your land there is a sacred field of great religious merit throughout the three worlds, / known as Hāṭakeśvara; and there is an auspicious sacred ford there, / celebrated as Śaṅkhatīrtha, which destroys all sins.

5.208.s:
yastatra kurute snānaṃ śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ ..
aṣṭamyāṃ śuklapakṣasya saṃprāpte māsi mādhave .. 44 ..
5.208.d:
यस्तत्र कुरुते स्नानं श्रद्धया परया युतः ..
अष्टम्यां शुक्लपक्षस्य संप्राप्ते मासि माधवे .. 44 ..
5.208.m: Whoever performs ritual ablution there, endowed with supreme faith, / on the eighth lunar day of the bright fortnight, when the month of Mādhava arrives,

5.208.s:
sūryavāre tu samprāpte bhāskarasyodayaṃ prati ..
sarvakuṣṭhavinirmukto jāyate sūryasaṃnibhaḥ .. 45 ..
5.208.d:
सूर्यवारे तु सम्प्राप्ते भास्करस्योदयं प्रति ..
सर्वकुष्ठविनिर्मुक्तो जायते सूर्यसंनिभः .. 45 ..
5.208.m: and when it falls on a Sunday, at the rising of the sun, / is freed from all leprosy and becomes like the sun.

5.208.s:
yaṃyaṃ kāmamabhidhyāyettaṃtaṃ sarveṣu durlabham ..
sa tadā''pnotyasaṃdigdhaṃ dṛṣṭvā śaṃkheśvaraṃ śubham.. 46 ..
5.208.d:
यंयं काममभिध्यायेत्तंतं सर्वेषु दुर्लभम् ..
स तदा'ऽप्नोत्यसंदिग्धं दृष्ट्वा शंखेश्वरं शुभम्.. 46 ..
5.208.m: Whatever desire one may contemplate, though most difficult to attain among all things, / one then obtains it beyond doubt after seeing the auspicious Śaṅkheśvara.

5.208.s:
kiṃ tvayā na śrutaṃ tatra svadeśe vasatā nṛpa ..
tasya tīrthasya māhātmyaṃ yattvamatra samāgataḥ ..47..
5.208.d:
किं त्वया न श्रुतं तत्र स्वदेशे वसता नृप ..
तस्य तीर्थस्य माहात्म्यं यत्त्वमत्र समागतः ..47..
5.208.m: Did you not hear of it, O king, while living there in your own realm— / the māhātmya of that sacred ford—that you have come here?

5.208.s:
.. siddhasena uvāca .. ..
kathaṃ śaṃkheśvaro devaḥ saṃjāto vada sanmune .. 48 ..
5.208.d:
.. सिद्धसेन उवाच .. ..
कथं शंखेश्वरो देवः संजातो वद सन्मुने .. 48 ..
5.208.m: Siddhasena said: / Tell me, O virtuous sage, how did the god Śaṅkheśvara come to be?

5.208.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
ahaṃ te kathayiṣyāmi kathāmetāṃ purātanīm ..
yathā śaṃkheśvaro jātaḥ śaṃkhatīrthaṃ tu pārthiva.. 49 ..
5.208.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
अहं ते कथयिष्यामि कथामेतां पुरातनीम् ..
यथा शंखेश्वरो जातः शंखतीर्थं तु पार्थिव.. 49 ..
5.208.m: Nārada said: / I shall tell you this ancient tale / of how Śaṅkheśvara arose, and also Śaṅkhatīrtha, O king.

5.208.s:
āsaturbrāhmaṇau pūrvaṃ likhitaḥ śaṃkha eva ca ..
bhrātarau vedaviduṣau tapasyugre vyavasthitau .. 6.209.50 ..
5.208.d:
आसतुर्ब्राह्मणौ पूर्वं लिखितः शंख एव च ..
भ्रातरौ वेदविदुषौ तपस्युग्रे व्यवस्थितौ .. 6.209.50 ..
5.208.m: Formerly there were two brahmins, Likhita and Śaṅkha, / brothers learned in the Vedas, devoted to fierce austerity.

5.208.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya likhitasyāśramaṃ prati ..
bhrāturjyeṣṭhasya saṃprāpto namaskārakṛte nṛpa ..51..
5.208.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य लिखितस्याश्रमं प्रति ..
भ्रातुर्ज्येष्ठस्य संप्राप्तो नमस्कारकृते नृप ..51..
5.208.m: Then, after some time, [Śaṅkha] went to the hermitage of Likhita, / his elder brother, in order to pay him homage, O king.

5.208.s: so'paśyadāśramaṃ śūnyaṃ likhitena vivarjitam ..52..
5.208.d: सोऽपश्यदाश्रमं शून्यं लिखितेन विवर्जितम् ..52..
5.208.m: He found the hermitage deserted, abandoned by Likhita.

5.208.s:
athāpaśyadvane tasmi nparipakvaphalāni saḥ ..
praṇayātpratijagrāha matvā bhrāturnṛpā''śramam ..53..
5.208.d:
अथापश्यद्वने तस्मि न्परिपक्वफलानि सः ..
प्रणयात्प्रतिजग्राह मत्वा भ्रातुर्नृपा'ऽश्रमम् ..53..
5.208.m: Then he saw fully ripe fruits in that forest; / out of affection, thinking it his brother's hermitage, O king, he took them.

5.208.s:
etasminnantare prāpto likhitastatra cāśrame..
yāvatpaśyati śaṃkhaṃ sa pragṛhī tabṛhatphalam..54..
5.208.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे प्राप्तो लिखितस्तत्र चाश्रमे..
यावत्पश्यति शंखं स प्रगृही तबृहत्फलम्..54..
5.208.m: In the meantime, Likhita arrived there at the hermitage / and saw Śaṅkha holding a large fruit.

5.208.s:
kimidaṃ vihitaṃ pāpa pāpaṃ sādhuvigarhitam ..
cauryakarma tvayā niṃdyaṃ yaddhṛtāni phalāni ca ..55..
5.208.d:
किमिदं विहितं पाप पापं साधुविगर्हितम् ..
चौर्यकर्म त्वया निंद्यं यद्धृतानि फलानि च ..55..
5.208.m: “What is this sin you have committed, O sinner, condemned by the virtuous? / A reprehensible act of theft has been done by you, in that fruits were taken!

5.208.s:
anena karmaṇā tubhyaṃ tapo yāsya ti saṃkṣayam..
cauryakarmapravṛttasya brāhmaṇairgarhitasya ca ..56..
5.208.d:
अनेन कर्मणा तुभ्यं तपो यास्य ति संक्षयम्..
चौर्यकर्मप्रवृत्तस्य ब्राह्मणैर्गर्हितस्य च ..56..
5.208.m: By this deed your austerity will come to an end, / since you have engaged in an act of theft and been censured by brahmins!”

5.208.s:
.. śaṃkha uvāca .. ..
ekodarasamutpanno jyeṣṭhabhrātā yathā pitā ..
bhūyāditi śrutirloke prasiddhā sarvataḥ sthitā .. 57 ..
5.208.d:
.. शंख उवाच .. ..
एकोदरसमुत्पन्नो ज्येष्ठभ्राता यथा पिता ..
भूयादिति श्रुतिर्लोके प्रसिद्धा सर्वतः स्थिता .. 57 ..
5.208.m: Śaṅkha said: / “An elder brother born of the same womb should be like a father: / so stands the well-known sacred tradition established everywhere in the world.

5.208.s:
tatkiṃ putrasya viprendra nādhikāraḥ piturdhane ..
yathaivaṃ niṣṭhurairvākyairnirbhartsayasi māṃ vibho .. 58 .. ..
5.208.d:
तत्किं पुत्रस्य विप्रेन्द्र नाधिकारः पितुर्धने ..
यथैवं निष्ठुरैर्वाक्यैर्निर्भर्त्सयसि मां विभो .. 58 .. ..
5.208.m: Has a son no right, then, O best of brahmins, to his father's property, / that you rebuke me thus with harsh words, O lord?”

5.208.s:
.. likhita uvāca .. ..
na doṣo jāyate hartuḥ putrasyātra kathaṃcana ..
ekatra saṃsthitasyātra piturvittamasaṃśayam .. 59 ..
5.208.d:
.. लिखित उवाच .. ..
न दोषो जायते हर्तुः पुत्रस्यात्र कथंचन ..
एकत्र संस्थितस्यात्र पितुर्वित्तमसंशयम् .. 59 ..
5.208.m: Likhita said: / “No fault arises in any way for a son who takes, / while living together [with him], his father's property, without doubt.

5.208.s:
vibhaktastu yadā putro bhrātā vā'pahareddhanam..
tadā doṣamavāpnoti cauryotthaṃ matameva me .. 6.209.60 ..
5.208.d:
विभक्तस्तु यदा पुत्रो भ्राता वाऽपहरेद्धनम्..
तदा दोषमवाप्नोति चौर्योत्थं मतमेव मे .. 6.209.60 ..
5.208.m: But when a son or a brother who has separated takes property, / then he incurs the fault arising from theft—such is my view.

5.208.s:
putrasya tu punarvittaṃ pitā harati sarvadā ..
na tasya vidyate doṣo vibhakta syāpi karhicit.. 61 ..
5.208.d:
पुत्रस्य तु पुनर्वित्तं पिता हरति सर्वदा ..
न तस्य विद्यते दोषो विभक्त स्यापि कर्हिचित्.. 61 ..
5.208.m: Moreover, a father may always take the property of his son; / for him there is no fault ever, even if [the son] is separated.

5.208.s:
atra ślokaḥ purā gīto manunā smṛtikāriṇā ..
taṃ te'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi dharmaśāstrodbhavaṃ vacaḥ .. 62 ..
5.208.d:
अत्र श्लोकः पुरा गीतो मनुना स्मृतिकारिणा ..
तं तेऽहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि धर्मशास्त्रोद्भवं वचः .. 62 ..
5.208.m: On this matter a verse was formerly sung by Manu, the author of the Smṛti; / I shall recite to you that statement originating in the Dharmaśāstra:

5.208.s:
traya evādhaproktā bhāryā dāsastathā sutaḥ ..
yatte samadhigacchaṃti yasya te tasya taddhanam .. 63 ..
5.208.d:
त्रय एवाधप्रोक्ता भार्या दासस्तथा सुतः ..
यत्ते समधिगच्छंति यस्य ते तस्य तद्धनम् .. 63 ..
5.208.m: ‘Three alone are declared to have no property: a wife, a servant, and a son; / whatever they acquire belongs to the one to whom they belong.’

5.208.s:
.. śaṃkha uvāca .. ..
yadyevaṃ cauryadoṣo'sti mama tāta mahattaraḥ..
nigrahaṃ kuru me śīghraṃ yena na syāttapaḥkṣayaḥ..64..
5.208.d:
.. शंख उवाच .. ..
यद्येवं चौर्यदोषोऽस्ति मम तात महत्तरः..
निग्रहं कुरु मे शीघ्रं येन न स्यात्तपःक्षयः..64..
5.208.m: Śaṅkha said: / “If indeed I have incurred such a grave fault of theft, my brother, / then punish me swiftly, so that my austerity may not be lost.”

5.208.s:
viśvāmitra uvāca..
tasya taṃ niścayaṃ jñātvā śastramādāya nirmalam..
cakartātha bhujau tasya bhrātā bhrātuśca nirghṛṇaḥ..
sopi cchinnakaro vipro vyathayāpi samanvitaḥ..65..
5.208.d:
विश्वामित्र उवाच..
तस्य तं निश्चयं ज्ञात्वा शस्त्रमादाय निर्मलम्..
चकर्ताथ भुजौ तस्य भ्राता भ्रातुश्च निर्घृणः..
सोपि च्छिन्नकरो विप्रो व्यथयापि समन्वितः..65..
5.208.m: Viśvāmitra said: / Knowing his resolve, taking up a clean blade, / the brother pitilessly severed both his brother's arms. / And that brahmin, though his hands were cut off and he was filled with agony,

5.208.s: manyamānaḥ prasādaṃ taṃ bhrāturjyeṣṭhasya pārthiva .. 66 ..
5.208.d: मन्यमानः प्रसादं तं भ्रातुर्ज्येष्ठस्य पार्थिव .. 66 ..
5.208.m: considered it the grace of his elder brother, O king.

5.208.s:
tatastu kāmadaṃ kṣetraṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñitam ..
matvā prāpya tapastepe kaṃcitprāpya jalāśayam .. 67 ..
5.208.d:
ततस्तु कामदं क्षेत्रं हाटकेश्वरसंज्ञितम् ..
मत्वा प्राप्य तपस्तेपे कंचित्प्राप्य जलाशयम् .. 67 ..
5.208.m: Then, knowing the sacred field called Hāṭakeśvara to be wish-fulfilling, / he went there, reached a certain body of water, and practiced austerity.

5.208.s:
varṣāsvākāśaśāyī ca hemante salilāśrayaḥ ..
pañcāgnisādhako grīṣme ṣaṣṭhakālakṛtāśanaḥ .. 68 ..
5.208.d:
वर्षास्वाकाशशायी च हेमन्ते सलिलाश्रयः ..
पञ्चाग्निसाधको ग्रीष्मे षष्ठकालकृताशनः .. 68 ..
5.208.m: He slept under the open sky in the rainy season, took refuge in the water in winter, / practiced the five-fire penance in summer, eating only at the sixth mealtime.

5.208.s:
saṃsnāpya bhāskaraṃ sthāṇuṃ tatpuraḥ śatarudriyam ..
japansāmoktarudrāṃśca bhava rudrāṃstathā japan ..
prāṇarudrāṃstathā nīlānskandasūktasamanvitān .. 69 ..
5.208.d:
संस्नाप्य भास्करं स्थाणुं तत्पुरः शतरुद्रियम् ..
जपन्सामोक्तरुद्रांश्च भव रुद्रांस्तथा जपन् ..
प्राणरुद्रांस्तथा नीलान्स्कन्दसूक्तसमन्वितान् .. 69 ..
5.208.m: Bathing the sun and the Sthāṇu [liṅga], before it chanting the Śatarudrīya, / chanting the Rudra mantras taught in the Sāmaveda, and chanting the Bhava-rudras, / the Prāṇa-rudras, and the Nīla mantras along with the Skandasūkta.

5.208.s:
tato varṣasahasrāṃte tuṣṭastasya maheśvaraḥ ..
provāca darśanaṃ gatvā saha sūrya vṛṣeśvaraiḥ .. 6.209.70 ..
5.208.d:
ततो वर्षसहस्रांते तुष्टस्तस्य महेश्वरः ..
प्रोवाच दर्शनं गत्वा सह सूर्य वृषेश्वरैः .. 6.209.70 ..
5.208.m: Then, at the end of a thousand years, Maheśvara was pleased with him; / he granted him darśana and spoke, together with the sun and the lords of bulls:

5.208.s:
.. maheśvara uvāca .. ..
śaṃkha tuṣṭo'smi te vatsa tapasānena suvrata ..
tasmātkathaya me kṣipraṃ yaddadāmi tavā'dhunā .. 71 ..
5.208.d:
.. महेश्वर उवाच .. ..
शंख तुष्टोऽस्मि ते वत्स तपसानेन सुव्रत ..
तस्मात्कथय मे क्षिप्रं यद्ददामि तवाऽधुना .. 71 ..
5.208.m: Maheśvara said: / “O Śaṅkha, I am pleased with you, my child, by this austerity, O one of noble vows! / Therefore tell me quickly what I may give you now.”

5.208.s:
.. .. śaṃkha uvāca .. ..
yadi tuṣṭo'si me deva yadi deyo varo mama ..
jāyetāṃ tādṛśau hastau yādṛśo me purā sthitau .. 72 ..
5.208.d:
.. .. शंख उवाच .. ..
यदि तुष्टोऽसि मे देव यदि देयो वरो मम ..
जायेतां तादृशौ हस्तौ यादृशो मे पुरा स्थितौ .. 72 ..
5.208.m: Śaṅkha said: / “If you are pleased with me, O god, if a boon is to be granted to me, / let both of my hands become just as they were formerly.

5.208.s:
tvayā'traiva sadā vāsaḥ kāryaḥ suravareśvara ..
liṃge kṛtvā dayāṃ deva mamopari mahattarām .. 73 ..
5.208.d:
त्वयाऽत्रैव सदा वासः कार्यः सुरवरेश्वर ..
लिंगे कृत्वा दयां देव ममोपरि महत्तराम् .. 73 ..
5.208.m: And you must always abide right here, O Lord of the foremost gods, / taking great compassion upon me in this liṅga, O god!

5.208.s:
etajjalāśayaṃ nātha mama nāmnā dharātale ..
prasiddhiṃ yātu lokasya yāvaccandrārkatārakāḥ .. 74 ..
5.208.d:
एतज्जलाशयं नाथ मम नाम्ना धरातले ..
प्रसिद्धिं यातु लोकस्य यावच्चन्द्रार्कतारकाः .. 74 ..
5.208.m: May this body of water on the surface of the earth become renowned / by my name among the people, as long as the moon, sun, and stars endure.

5.208.s:
atra yaḥ kurute snānaṃ dhṛtvā manasi durlabham ..
kiṃcidvastu samagraṃ tu tasya saṃpatsyate vibho .. 75 .. ..
5.208.d:
अत्र यः कुरुते स्नानं धृत्वा मनसि दुर्लभम् ..
किंचिद्वस्तु समग्रं तु तस्य संपत्स्यते विभो .. 75 .. ..
5.208.m: Whoever performs ritual ablution here, holding in mind some desired thing / difficult to obtain, let all of it be accomplished for him, O omnipresent Lord!”

5.208.s:
.. śrībhagavānuvāca .. ..
adyāhaṃ darśanaṃ prāptastava caivāṣṭamīdine ..
mādhavasya site pakṣe yasmādbrāhmaṇasattama .. 76 ..
5.208.d:
.. श्रीभगवानुवाच .. ..
अद्याहं दर्शनं प्राप्तस्तव चैवाष्टमीदिने ..
माधवस्य सिते पक्षे यस्माद्ब्राह्मणसत्तम .. 76 ..
5.208.m: The Blessed Lord said: / “Since I have appeared to your sight this day, / on the eighth lunar day of the bright fortnight of the month of Mādhava, O best of brahmins,

5.208.s:
tasmātsaṃkramaṇaṃ liṃge tāvake'smindvijottama ..
kariṣyāmi na sandeho dinamekamasaṃśayam .. 77 ..
5.208.d:
तस्मात्संक्रमणं लिंगे तावकेऽस्मिन्द्विजोत्तम ..
करिष्यामि न सन्देहो दिनमेकमसंशयम् .. 77 ..
5.208.m: therefore, O highest of brahmins, I will certainly make my entry / into this liṅga of yours for one day; of this there is no doubt.

5.208.s:
yaścātra divase prāpte tīrthe'traiva bhavodbhave ..
snānaṃ kṛtvā ravervāra udayaṃ samupasthite .. 78 ..
5.208.d:
यश्चात्र दिवसे प्राप्ते तीर्थेऽत्रैव भवोद्भवे ..
स्नानं कृत्वा रवेर्वार उदयं समुपस्थिते .. 78 ..
5.208.m: And on the arrival of that day, whoever performs ritual ablution / right here at this sacred ford born of Bhava, on a Sunday at sunrise,

5.208.s:
pūjayiṣyati me mūrtiṃ tvayā saṃsthāpitāṃ dvija ..
kuṣṭhavyādhivinirmukto mama lokaṃ sa yāsyati .. 79 ..
5.208.d:
पूजयिष्यति मे मूर्तिं त्वया संस्थापितां द्विज ..
कुष्ठव्याधिविनिर्मुक्तो मम लोकं स यास्यति .. 79 ..
5.208.m: and worships my form installed by you, O brahmin, / shall be freed from the disease of leprosy and shall go to my world.

5.208.s:
śeṣakāle'pi viprendra ajñānavihitādaghāt ..
muktiṃ prāpsyatyasaṃdigdhaṃ mama vākyāddvijottama .. 6.209.80 ..
5.208.d:
शेषकालेऽपि विप्रेन्द्र अज्ञानविहितादघात् ..
मुक्तिं प्राप्स्यत्यसंदिग्धं मम वाक्याद्द्विजोत्तम .. 6.209.80 ..
5.208.m: Even at the end of life, O foremost of brahmins, from sin committed in ignorance / one will surely attain liberation by my word, O highest of brahmins.

5.208.s:
tathā tavāpi yau hastau chinnāvetāvubhāvapi ..
tasminyoge'bhiṣekāttauḥ syātāṃ bhūyo'pi tādṛśau .. 81 ..
5.208.d:
तथा तवापि यौ हस्तौ छिन्नावेतावुभावपि ..
तस्मिन्योगेऽभिषेकात्तौः स्यातां भूयोऽपि तादृशौ .. 81 ..
5.208.m: Likewise, these two arms of yours that were cut off— / by ritual sprinkling in that planetary conjunction, both shall again become as they were.

5.208.s:
eṣa me pratyayo vipra bhaviṣyati tavā'dhunā ..
bhūyaḥ snānaṃ vidhāya tvaṃ tato mūrtiṃ mamārcaya .. 82 ..
5.208.d:
एष मे प्रत्ययो विप्र भविष्यति तवाऽधुना ..
भूयः स्नानं विधाय त्वं ततो मूर्तिं ममार्चय .. 82 ..
5.208.m: This assurance of mine shall be yours right now, O brahmin: / having performed ritual ablution once again, then worship my form.

5.208.s:
anye'pi vyaṃgatāṃ prāptāḥ saṃyoge'tra tava sthite ..
snātvā māṃ pūjayiṣyaṃti muktiṃ yāsyaṃti te dvija .. .. 83 ..
5.208.d:
अन्येऽपि व्यंगतां प्राप्ताः संयोगेऽत्र तव स्थिते ..
स्नात्वा मां पूजयिष्यंति मुक्तिं यास्यंति ते द्विज .. .. 83 ..
5.208.m: Others too who have suffered mutilation, when this conjunction of yours is present, / upon bathing and worshipping me, shall attain liberation, O brahmin.”

5.208.s:
evamuktvā sahasrāṃśustataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ ..
śaṃkho'pi tatkṣaṇātsnātvā pūjayitvā divākaram .. 84 ..
5.208.d:
एवमुक्त्वा सहस्रांशुस्ततश्चादर्शनं गतः ..
शंखोऽपि तत्क्षणात्स्नात्वा पूजयित्वा दिवाकरम् .. 84 ..
5.208.m: Having spoken thus, the thousand-rayed Sun disappeared from sight. / Śaṅkha too, having immediately taken a ritual ablution and worshipped the Sun,

5.208.s:
yāvatpaśyati cātmānaṃ tāvaddhastasamanvitam ..
ātmānaṃ paśyamānastu vismayaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ .. 85 ..
5.208.d:
यावत्पश्यति चात्मानं तावद्धस्तसमन्वितम् ..
आत्मानं पश्यमानस्तु विस्मयं परमं गतः .. 85 ..
5.208.m: as soon as he looked at himself, saw that he had his hands. / Looking at himself, he was filled with supreme wonder.

5.208.s:
tataḥprabhṛti tatraiva kṛtvā''śramapadaṃ nṛpa ..
tapastepe dvija śreṣṭho gataśca paramāṃ gatim .. 86 ..
5.208.d:
ततःप्रभृति तत्रैव कृत्वा'ऽश्रमपदं नृप ..
तपस्तेपे द्विज श्रेष्ठो गतश्च परमां गतिम् .. 86 ..
5.208.m: From that time forward, O king, having established a hermitage right there, / that best of brahmins performed austerities and attained the supreme goal.

5.208.s:
tasmāttvamapi rājeṃdra saṃyogaṃ prāpya tattvataḥ ..
tenaiva vidhinā snātvā tvaṃ pūjaya divākaram .. 87 ..
5.208.d:
तस्मात्त्वमपि राजेंद्र संयोगं प्राप्य तत्त्वतः ..
तेनैव विधिना स्नात्वा त्वं पूजय दिवाकरम् .. 87 ..
5.208.m: Therefore, O king of kings, you too, having arrived at that conjunction in accordance with reality, / having taken a ritual ablution by that very procedure, worship the Sun.

5.208.s:
yaścaitacchṛṇuyānnityaṃ paṭhedvā purato raveḥ ..
tasyānvaye'pi no kuṣṭhī kadācitsamprajāyate .. 88 ..
5.208.d:
यश्चैतच्छृणुयान्नित्यं पठेद्वा पुरतो रवेः ..
तस्यान्वयेऽपि नो कुष्ठी कदाचित्सम्प्रजायते .. 88 ..
5.208.m: And whoever hears this constantly or recites it before the Sun, / in his lineage too, a leper is never born.

5.208.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyā ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śaṃkhādityaśaṃkhatīrthotpattivṛttāṃtavarṇanaṃnāma navottaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 209 .. .. ..
5.208.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहिताया षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शंखादित्यशंखतीर्थोत्पत्तिवृत्तांतवर्णनंनाम नवोत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 209 .. .. ..
5.208.m: Thus ends the two hundred and ninth chapter, named 'Description of the Origin of Śaṅkhāditya and Śaṅkhatīrtha', in the Māhātmya of the Hāṭakeśvara Field, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [section], of the Mahāpurāṇa composed by Skanda consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.209.s:
.. .. viśvāmitra uvāca .. ..
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya devarṣernāradasya ca ..
siddhaseno mahīpālaḥ prāpya taṃ yogamuttamam .. 1 ..
5.209.d:
.. .. विश्वामित्र उवाच .. ..
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य देवर्षेर्नारदस्य च ..
सिद्धसेनो महीपालः प्राप्य तं योगमुत्तमम् .. 1 ..
5.209.m: Viśvāmitra said: / Having heard those words of that celestial seer Nārada, / King Siddhasena, having attained that supreme conjunction,

5.209.s:
mādhave māsi saṃprāpte aṣṭamyāṃ sūryavāsare ..
sūryodaye tu saṃprāpte yāvatsnātvā'rcayedravim ..2..
5.209.d:
माधवे मासि संप्राप्ते अष्टम्यां सूर्यवासरे ..
सूर्योदये तु संप्राप्ते यावत्स्नात्वाऽर्चयेद्रविम् ..2..
5.209.m: when the month of Mādhava arrived, on the eighth day [of the lunar fortnight], on a Sunday, / at the rise of the sun, as soon as he had bathed and worshipped the Sun,

5.209.s:
tāvatkuṣṭhavinirmuktaḥ sahasā samapadyata ..
tato divyavapurbhūtvā santoṣaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ .. 3 ..
5.209.d:
तावत्कुष्ठविनिर्मुक्तः सहसा समपद्यत ..
ततो दिव्यवपुर्भूत्वा सन्तोषं परमं गतः .. 3 ..
5.209.m: he was instantly freed from leprosy. / Having then obtained a divine body, he experienced supreme contentment.

5.209.s:
prāyaścittaṃ tataścakre tāṃbūlasya ca bhakṣaṇam ..
ajñānena kṛtaṃ yacca cūrṇapatrasamanvitam .. 4 ..
5.209.d:
प्रायश्चित्तं ततश्चक्रे तांबूलस्य च भक्षणम् ..
अज्ञानेन कृतं यच्च चूर्णपत्रसमन्वितम् .. 4 ..
5.209.m: He then performed expiation for the consumption of betel, / which, along with the leaf and lime, he had done out of ignorance.

5.209.s:
tataśca paramāṃ lakṣmīṃ saṃprāptaḥ sa mahīpatiḥ ..
pitṛpaitāmahaṃ rājyaṃ sa pracakre yathā purā .. 5 ..
5.209.d:
ततश्च परमां लक्ष्मीं संप्राप्तः स महीपतिः ..
पितृपैतामहं राज्यं स प्रचक्रे यथा पुरा .. 5 ..
5.209.m: And then that ruler of the earth attained supreme prosperity; / he administered his ancestral kingdom just as before.

5.209.s:
etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ śaṃkhatīrthasamudbhavam ..
māhātmyaṃ pārthivaśreṣṭha kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumi cchasi .. 6 ..
5.209.d:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं शंखतीर्थसमुद्भवम् ..
माहात्म्यं पार्थिवश्रेष्ठ किं भूयः श्रोतुमि च्छसि .. 6 ..
5.209.m: All this māhātmya arising from Śaṅkhatīrtha has been told to you, / O best of kings. What more do you wish to hear?

5.209.s:
.. ānarta uvāca .. ..
atyāścaryamidaṃ brahmanyattvayā parikīrtitam ..
yallakṣmīstasya sannaṣṭā cūrṇapatrasya bhakṣaṇāt .. 7 ..
5.209.d:
.. आनर्त उवाच .. ..
अत्याश्चर्यमिदं ब्रह्मन्यत्त्वया परिकीर्तितम् ..
यल्लक्ष्मीस्तस्य सन्नष्टा चूर्णपत्रस्य भक्षणात् .. 7 ..
5.209.m: Ānarta said: / This is most wondrous, O holy one, which you have proclaimed, / that his fortune was destroyed because of consuming the leaf with lime.

5.209.s:
kīdṛktena kṛtaṃ tasya prāyaścittaṃ viśuddhayre ..
kīdṛktena kṛtaṃ tacca nijarājyaṃ yathā purā.. 8 ..
5.209.d:
कीदृक्तेन कृतं तस्य प्रायश्चित्तं विशुद्धय्रे ..
कीदृक्तेन कृतं तच्च निजराज्यं यथा पुरा.. 8 ..
5.209.m: What kind of expiation was performed by him for purification? / And how did he restore his own kingdom as before?

5.209.s:
.. viśvāmitra uvāca .. ..
eṣā puṇyatamā medhyā nāgavallī narādhipa ..
ayathāvatkṛtā vaktre bahūndoṣānprayacchati ..
tasmādyatnena saṃbhakṣyā dattvā caiva svaśaktitaḥ .. 9 ..
5.209.d:
.. विश्वामित्र उवाच .. ..
एषा पुण्यतमा मेध्या नागवल्ली नराधिप ..
अयथावत्कृता वक्त्रे बहून्दोषान्प्रयच्छति ..
तस्माद्यत्नेन संभक्ष्या दत्त्वा चैव स्वशक्तितः .. 9 ..
5.209.m: Viśvāmitra said: / This betel vine is most meritorious and pure, O ruler of men; / [yet] consumed improperly in the mouth, it brings many faults. / Therefore, it should be consumed with care, and after giving according to one's capacity.

5.209.s:
.. ānarta uvāca .. ..
nāgavallī kathaṃ jātā kasmāddoṣo mahānsmṛtaḥ ..
ayathāvadbhakṣaṇācca tanme vaktumihārhasi .. 6.210.10 ..
5.209.d:
.. आनर्त उवाच .. ..
नागवल्ली कथं जाता कस्माद्दोषो महान्स्मृतः ..
अयथावद्भक्षणाच्च तन्मे वक्तुमिहार्हसि .. 6.210.10 ..
5.209.m: Ānarta said: / How was the betel vine born? Why is it considered a great fault / to eat it improperly? You ought to tell me this now.

5.209.s:
.. viśvāmitra uvāca .. ..
praśnabhāro mahāneṣa tvayā me parikīrtitaḥ ..
tathāpi ca vadiṣyāmi yadi te kautukaṃ nṛpa ..
yasmātsañjāyate doṣaścūrṇapatrasya bhakṣaṇāt.. 11 ..
5.209.d:
.. विश्वामित्र उवाच .. ..
प्रश्नभारो महानेष त्वया मे परिकीर्तितः ..
तथापि च वदिष्यामि यदि ते कौतुकं नृप ..
यस्मात्सञ्जायते दोषश्चूर्णपत्रस्य भक्षणात्.. 11 ..
5.209.m: Viśvāmitra said: / This is a heavy burden of questions that has been set forth to me by you; / nevertheless, I shall tell you, O king, if you are curious, / why fault arises from consuming the leaf with lime.

5.209.s:
amṛtārthaṃ purā devairmathitaḥ kalaśodadhiḥ ..
manthānaṃ mandaraṃ kṛtvā netraṃ kṛtvā tu vāsukim .. 12 ..
5.209.d:
अमृतार्थं पुरा देवैर्मथितः कलशोदधिः ..
मन्थानं मन्दरं कृत्वा नेत्रं कृत्वा तु वासुकिम् .. 12 ..
5.209.m: Long ago, for the sake of nectar, the jar-like ocean was churned by the gods, / making Mandara the churning stick and Vāsuki the churning rope.

5.209.s:
mukhadeśe balirlagnaḥ pucchadeśe'khilāḥ surāḥ ..
vāsudevamatenaiva sandadhārātha kacchapaḥ .. 13 ..
5.209.d:
मुखदेशे बलिर्लग्नः पुच्छदेशेऽखिलाः सुराः ..
वासुदेवमतेनैव सन्दधाराथ कच्छपः .. 13 ..
5.209.m: Bali grasped the head region, and all the gods the tail region. / Then, by the counsel of Vāsudeva, the Tortoise supported [the mountain].

5.209.s:
mandare bhramamāṇe tu prāgeva nṛpasattama ..
ānarta sahasā jātaṃ ratnatritayameva ca .. 14 ..
5.209.d:
मन्दरे भ्रममाणे तु प्रागेव नृपसत्तम ..
आनर्त सहसा जातं रत्नत्रितयमेव च .. 14 ..
5.209.m: As Mandara was turning, O best of kings, / O Ānarta, a triad of jewels arose first of all, quite suddenly:

5.209.s:
nīlāṃbaradharaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ puruṣo vakranāsikaḥ ..
kṛṣṇadantaḥ sthūlaśirā dīrghagrīvo mahodaraḥ ..
śūrpākārāṃghrirevā'sau cipiṭākṣo bhayāvahaḥ .. 15 ..
5.209.d:
नीलांबरधरः कृष्णः पुरुषो वक्रनासिकः ..
कृष्णदन्तः स्थूलशिरा दीर्घग्रीवो महोदरः ..
शूर्पाकारांघ्रिरेवाऽसौ चिपिटाक्षो भयावहः .. 15 ..
5.209.m: A dark man clad in blue garments, with a crooked nose, / black teeth, a thick head, a long neck, a potbelly, / feet shaped like winnowing baskets, flat-eyed, and terrifying;

5.209.s:
tathā tadrūpiṇī tasya kubhāryā rākṣasī yathā ..
śiśunāṃgulilagnena garbhaśramaparāyaṇā .. 16 ..
5.209.d:
तथा तद्रूपिणी तस्य कुभार्या राक्षसी यथा ..
शिशुनांगुलिलग्नेन गर्भश्रमपरायणा .. 16 ..
5.209.m: likewise, a vile wife of the same form as his, like a demoness, / with a child clinging to her finger, exhausted by pregnancy.

5.209.s:
tato devagaṇāḥ sarve dānavāśca viśeṣataḥ ..
manthānaṃ tatparityajya tāngrahītuṃ pradhāvitāḥ .. 17 ..
5.209.d:
ततो देवगणाः सर्वे दानवाश्च विशेषतः ..
मन्थानं तत्परित्यज्य तान्ग्रहीतुं प्रधाविताः .. 17 ..
5.209.m: Then all the hosts of gods, and especially the Dānavas, / abandoning the churning stick, ran forward to seize them.

5.209.s:
atha tānvikṛtāndṛṣṭvā sarve śaṃkāsamanvitāḥ ..
jagṛhurnaiva rājeṃdra jahasuśca parasparam .. 18 ..
5.209.d:
अथ तान्विकृतान्दृष्ट्वा सर्वे शंकासमन्विताः ..
जगृहुर्नैव राजेंद्र जहसुश्च परस्परम् .. 18 ..
5.209.m: Then, seeing them deformed, filled with hesitation, / they did not seize them, O king of kings, and laughed among themselves.

5.209.s:
athovāca balirdaityaḥ kṛtāṃjalipuṭaḥ sthitaḥ ..
brahmā''di yallabhetsarvaṃ yatpurastātprajāyate .. 19 ..
5.209.d:
अथोवाच बलिर्दैत्यः कृतांजलिपुटः स्थितः ..
ब्रह्मा'ऽदि यल्लभेत्सर्वं यत्पुरस्तात्प्रजायते .. 19 ..
5.209.m: Then the Daitya Bali, standing with palms joined in reverence, said: / 'Whatever is produced first, let Brahmā and the others receive it all.

5.209.s:
ratnatritayametaddhi tasmādgṛhṇātu padmajaḥ ..
yena siddhirbhavedasminmanthane kasya cā'rpaṇāt .. 6.210.20 ..
5.209.d:
रत्नत्रितयमेतद्धि तस्माद्गृह्णातु पद्मजः ..
येन सिद्धिर्भवेदस्मिन्मन्थने कस्य चाऽर्पणात् .. 6.210.20 ..
5.209.m: Therefore, let the lotus-born [Brahmā] take this triad of jewels, / so that there may be success in this churning upon offering it to someone.'

5.209.s:
tadvākyaṃ viṣṇunā tasya śaṃsitaṃ śaṃkareṇa tu ..
iṃdrādyaiśca suraiḥ sarvairdānavaiśca viśeṣataḥ 21..
5.209.d:
तद्वाक्यं विष्णुना तस्य शंसितं शंकरेण तु ..
इंद्राद्यैश्च सुरैः सर्वैर्दानवैश्च विशेषतः 21..
5.209.m: That speech of his was praised by Viṣṇu, by Śaṃkara, / by all the gods headed by Indra, and especially by the Dānavas.

5.209.s:
etasminnaṃtare brahmā jagrāha tritayaṃ ca tat..
dākṣiṇyātsarvadevānāmanicchannapi pārthiva ..
mamanthuḥ sāgaraṃ rājanpunaste yatnamāśritāḥ .. 22 ..
5.209.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे ब्रह्मा जग्राह त्रितयं च तत्..
दाक्षिण्यात्सर्वदेवानामनिच्छन्नपि पार्थिव ..
ममन्थुः सागरं राजन्पुनस्ते यत्नमाश्रिताः .. 22 ..
5.209.m: In the meantime, Brahmā took that triad / out of courtesy toward all the gods, O king, even though unwilling. / Resorting to effort again, O king, they churned the ocean.

5.209.s:
tataśca vāruṇī jātā divyagandhasamanvitā ..
balinā saṃgṛhītā sā pratyakṣaṃ balavidviṣaḥ .. 23 ..
5.209.d:
ततश्च वारुणी जाता दिव्यगन्धसमन्विता ..
बलिना संगृहीता सा प्रत्यक्षं बलविद्विषः .. 23 ..
5.209.m: Then Vāruṇī arose, endowed with divine fragrance; / she was seized by Bali right before the eyes of the enemy of Bala [Indra].

5.209.s:
āvarte cāpare jāte niṣkrāṃtaḥ kaustubho maṇiḥ ..
sa gṛhīto mahārāja viṣṇunā prabhaviṣṇunā .. 24 ..
5.209.d:
आवर्ते चापरे जाते निष्क्रांतः कौस्तुभो मणिः ..
स गृहीतो महाराज विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना .. 24 ..
5.209.m: And when another whirlpool arose, the Kaustubha gem came forth; / it was taken, O great king, by the all-powerful Viṣṇu.

5.209.s:
athāpare sthite tatra mahāvarte niśāpatiḥ ..
sañjātaḥ sa vṛṣāṃkena saṃgṛhītaśca tatkṣaṇāt .. 25 ..
5.209.d:
अथापरे स्थिते तत्र महावर्ते निशापतिः ..
सञ्जातः स वृषांकेन संगृहीतश्च तत्क्षणात् .. 25 ..
5.209.m: Then, as another great whirlpool remained there, the Moon was born, / and he was seized immediately by the Bull-bannered [Śiva].

5.209.s:
pārijātastato jāto divyagandhasamanvitaḥ ..
sa gṛhītvā suraiḥ sarvaiḥ sthāpito naṃdane vane .. 26 ..
5.209.d:
पारिजातस्ततो जातो दिव्यगन्धसमन्वितः ..
स गृहीत्वा सुरैः सर्वैः स्थापितो नंदने वने .. 26 ..
5.209.m: Then the Pārijāta tree arose, endowed with divine fragrance; / taken by all the gods, it was planted in the Nandana grove.

5.209.s:
tasyānaṃtaramevātha surabhī vatsasaṃyutā ..
niṣkrāṃtā vyomamārgeṇa golokaṃ samavasthitā .. 27 ..
5.209.d:
तस्यानंतरमेवाथ सुरभी वत्ससंयुता ..
निष्क्रांता व्योममार्गेण गोलोकं समवस्थिता .. 27 ..
5.209.m: Immediately after it, Surabhī along with her calf / came forth, and went via the sky to take up her abode in Goloka.

5.209.s:
tato dhanvaṃtarirjāto bibhraddhaste kamaṃḍalum ..
saṃpūrṇamamṛtenaiva sa devairdānavainṛpa .. 28 ..
5.209.d:
ततो धन्वंतरिर्जातो बिभ्रद्धस्ते कमंडलुम् ..
संपूर्णममृतेनैव स देवैर्दानवैनृप .. 28 ..
5.209.m: Then Dhanvantari was born, bearing in his hand a waterpot / completely filled with nectar, O king. / By the gods and Dānavas,

5.209.s:
gṛhīto yugapatkruddhaiḥ parasparajigīṣayā ..
devānāṃ hastago vaidyo daityānāṃ ca kamaṇḍaluḥ.. 29 ..
5.209.d:
गृहीतो युगपत्क्रुद्धैः परस्परजिगीषया ..
देवानां हस्तगो वैद्यो दैत्यानां च कमण्डलुः.. 29 ..
5.209.m: angered simultaneously with the desire to conquer one another, he was seized; / the physician fell into the hands of the gods, and the waterpot into the hands of the Daityas.

5.209.s:
tatastaṃ lobhasaṃyuktā mamaṃthuḥ sāgaraṃ nṛpa ..
padmahastātra saṃjātā tato lakṣmīḥ sitāṃbarā .. 6.210.30 ..
5.209.d:
ततस्तं लोभसंयुक्ता ममंथुः सागरं नृप ..
पद्महस्तात्र संजाता ततो लक्ष्मीः सितांबरा .. 6.210.30 ..
5.209.m: Filled with greed, they then churned the ocean, O king; / thereupon Lakṣmī was born with a lotus in her hand, clothed in white garments.

5.209.s:
svayameva vṛto viṣṇustayā pārthivasattama ..
mathyamāne tatotīva samudre devadānavaiḥ .. 31 ..
5.209.d:
स्वयमेव वृतो विष्णुस्तया पार्थिवसत्तम ..
मथ्यमाने ततोतीव समुद्रे देवदानवैः .. 31 ..
5.209.m: She chose Viṣṇu of her own accord, O best of kings. / Then, as the ocean was being churned exceedingly by the gods and Dānavas,

5.209.s:
kālakūṭaṃ samutpannaṃ yena sarve surāsurāḥ ..
saṃprāptāḥ paramaṃ kaṣṭaṃ prabhagnāśca diśo daśa .. 32 ..
5.209.d:
कालकूटं समुत्पन्नं येन सर्वे सुरासुराः ..
संप्राप्ताः परमं कष्टं प्रभग्नाश्च दिशो दश .. 32 ..
5.209.m: the Kālakūṭa poison arose, by which all the gods and Asuras / were brought to extreme distress and fled in the ten directions.

5.209.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhagavāñchaṃbhustīvraṃ tīvaparākramaḥ ..
bhakṣayāmāsa rājeṃdra nīlakaṇṭhastato'bhavat .. 33 ..
5.209.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा भगवाञ्छंभुस्तीव्रं तीवपराक्रमः ..
भक्षयामास राजेंद्र नीलकण्ठस्ततोऽभवत् .. 33 ..
5.209.m: Seeing that fierce poison, the lord Śambhu of fierce valor / swallowed it, O king of kings; thence he became blue-throated.

5.209.s:
atha saṃtyajya maṃthānaṃ maṃdaraṃ vāsukiṃ tathā ..
amṛtārthe'bhavadyuddhaṃ daityānāṃ vibudhaiḥ saha .. 34 ..
5.209.d:
अथ संत्यज्य मंथानं मंदरं वासुकिं तथा ..
अमृतार्थेऽभवद्युद्धं दैत्यानां विबुधैः सह .. 34 ..
5.209.m: Then, abandoning the churning stick Mandara as well as Vāsuki, / there was a battle between the Daityas and the gods for the sake of the nectar.

5.209.s:
atha strīrūpamādhāya viṣṇurdaityānuvāca tān ..
tato hṛṣṭo balistasyai dattvā pīyūṣameva tat .. 35 ..
5.209.d:
अथ स्त्रीरूपमाधाय विष्णुर्दैत्यानुवाच तान् ..
ततो हृष्टो बलिस्तस्यै दत्त्वा पीयूषमेव तत् .. 35 ..
5.209.m: Then Viṣṇu, assuming the form of a woman, spoke to those Daityas. / Then Bali, delighted, gave that very nectar to her. 35.

5.209.s:
viśvāsaṃ paramaṃ gatvā yuddhaṃ cakre suraiḥ saha ..
tato viṣṇuḥ parityajya strīrūpaṃ puruṣākṛtiḥ .. 36 ..
5.209.d:
विश्वासं परमं गत्वा युद्धं चक्रे सुरैः सह ..
ततो विष्णुः परित्यज्य स्त्रीरूपं पुरुषाकृतिः .. 36 ..
5.209.m: Placing supreme trust [in her], he fought with the gods. / Then Viṣṇu, casting off the female form, assumed a male appearance. 36.

5.209.s:
tadevāmṛtamādāya yayau yatra divaukasaḥ ..
abravīttānsuhṛṣṭātmā pivadhvamamṛtaṃ surāḥ .. 37 ..
5.209.d:
तदेवामृतमादाय ययौ यत्र दिवौकसः ..
अब्रवीत्तान्सुहृष्टात्मा पिवध्वममृतं सुराः .. 37 ..
5.209.m: Taking that very nectar, he went to where the gods were. / With a joyful heart, he said to them: 'Drink the nectar, O gods! 37.

5.209.s:
yenāmaratvamāsādya vyāpādayata dānavān ..
te tatheti pratijñāya papuḥ pīyūṣamuttamam .. 38 ..
5.209.d:
येनामरत्वमासाद्य व्यापादयत दानवान् ..
ते तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय पपुः पीयूषमुत्तमम् .. 38 ..
5.209.m: Attaining immortality through it, destroy the Dānavas!' / Agreeing with 'So be it,' they drank the supreme nectar. 38.

5.209.s: amarāśca tato jātā jaghnuḥ saṃkhye mahāsurān .. 39 ..
5.209.d: अमराश्च ततो जाता जघ्नुः संख्ये महासुरान् .. 39 ..
5.209.m: And having thus become immortal, they slew the great Asuras in battle. 39.

5.209.s:
teṣāṃ pānavidhau tatra vartamāne mahīpate ..
rāhurvibudharūpeṇa papau pīyūṣamutsukaḥ .. 6.210.40 ..
5.209.d:
तेषां पानविधौ तत्र वर्तमाने महीपते ..
राहुर्विबुधरूपेण पपौ पीयूषमुत्सुकः .. 6.210.40 ..
5.209.m: While their drinking rite was taking place there, O lord of the earth, / Rāhu, eager [for it], drank the nectar disguised as a god. 40.

5.209.s:
sa lakṣito mahādaityaścaṃdrārkābhyāṃ ca tatkṣaṇāt ..
nivedito hare rājannāyaṃ devo mahāsuraḥ .. .. 41 ..
5.209.d:
स लक्षितो महादैत्यश्चंद्रार्काभ्यां च तत्क्षणात् ..
निवेदितो हरे राजन्नायं देवो महासुरः .. .. 41 ..
5.209.m: That great Daitya was spotted at that moment by the moon and the sun, / and reported to Hari: 'O King, this is no god, but a great Asura!' 41.

5.209.s:
tacchrutvā vāsudevena tasya cakraṃ sudarśanam..
vadhāya pārthivaśreṣṭha muktaṃ vajrasamaprabham .. 42 ..
5.209.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वासुदेवेन तस्य चक्रं सुदर्शनम्..
वधाय पार्थिवश्रेष्ठ मुक्तं वज्रसमप्रभम् .. 42 ..
5.209.m: Hearing that, the Sudarśana discus, blazing like a thunderbolt, / was released by Vāsudeva to slay him, O best of earthly kings. 42.

5.209.s:
yāvanmātraṃ śarīraṃ tattasya vyāptaṃ mahīpate ..
amṛtena tataḥ kṛttamamoghenāpi tacchiraḥ .. 43 ..
tato'maratvamāpannaḥ sa yāvatsiṃhikāsutaḥ ..
tāvatprokto'cyutenātha sāmnā paramavalgunā .. 44 ..
tyaja daityānmahābhāga devānāṃ saṃmato bhava ..
saṃprāpsyasi parāṃ pūjāṃ sadā tvaṃ grahamaṃḍale .. 45 ..
5.209.d:
यावन्मात्रं शरीरं तत्तस्य व्याप्तं महीपते ..
अमृतेन ततः कृत्तममोघेनापि तच्छिरः .. 43 ..
ततोऽमरत्वमापन्नः स यावत्सिंहिकासुतः ..
तावत्प्रोक्तोऽच्युतेनाथ साम्ना परमवल्गुना .. 44 ..
त्यज दैत्यान्महाभाग देवानां संमतो भव ..
संप्राप्स्यसि परां पूजां सदा त्वं ग्रहमंडले .. 45 ..
5.209.m: O lord of the earth, to whatever extent his body had been permeated / by the nectar, his head was severed by that unfailing [discus]. 43. / But as that son of Siṃhikā had attained immortality, / Acyuta then spoke to him in the gentlest words of conciliation: 44. / 'Abandon the Daityas, O fortunate one; be well-disposed to the gods. / You shall always receive supreme worship within the circle of the planets.' 45.

5.209.s:
sa tatheti pratijñāya tyaktvā tāndaityasattamān ..
pūjāṃ prāpnoti martyānāṃ saṃsthito grahamaṇḍale .. 46 ..
5.209.d:
स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय त्यक्त्वा तान्दैत्यसत्तमान् ..
पूजां प्राप्नोति मर्त्यानां संस्थितो ग्रहमण्डले .. 46 ..
5.209.m: Agreeing with 'So be it' and leaving those foremost Daityas, / he abides in the planetary circle and receives the worship of mortals. 46.

5.209.s:
etasminnaṃtare daityā nirjitāḥ surasattamaiḥ ..
diśo jagmuḥ paritrastāḥ kecinmṛtyumupāgatāḥ .. 47 ..
5.209.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे दैत्या निर्जिताः सुरसत्तमैः ..
दिशो जग्मुः परित्रस्ताः केचिन्मृत्युमुपागताः .. 47 ..
5.209.m: In the meantime, vanquished by the foremost gods, / the Daityas fled in terror in all directions, and some met their death. 47.

5.209.s:
pītaśeṣaṃ ca pīyūṣaṃ sthāpitaṃ nandane vane ..
nāgarājasya yatraiva sthitamālānameva ca .. 48 ..
5.209.d:
पीतशेषं च पीयूषं स्थापितं नन्दने वने ..
नागराजस्य यत्रैव स्थितमालानमेव च .. 48 ..
5.209.m: The nectar that remained after drinking was placed in the Nandana grove, / at the very post where the lord of elephants was tethered. 48.

5.209.s:
aharniśaṃ madasrāvī karīṃdraḥ so'pi saṃsthitaḥ ..
tatprabhāvaiḥ prabhinnaḥ sa pīyūṣasya kamaṃḍaluḥ ..49..
5.209.d:
अहर्निशं मदस्रावी करींद्रः सोऽपि संस्थितः ..
तत्प्रभावैः प्रभिन्नः स पीयूषस्य कमंडलुः ..49..
5.209.m: That lord of elephants also stood there, exuding musth day and night; / [and] by its power, that water-pot of nectar was cracked open. 49.

5.209.s:
tato vallī samutpannā tasmāccaiva kamaṇḍaloḥ ..
tatrālānasamārūḍhā vṛddhiṃ ca paramāṃ gatā .. 6.210.50 ..
5.209.d:
ततो वल्ली समुत्पन्ना तस्माच्चैव कमण्डलोः ..
तत्रालानसमारूढा वृद्धिं च परमां गता .. 6.210.50 ..
5.209.m: From that water-pot a creeper was then born; / climbing up the tethering-post there, it grew exceedingly. 50.

5.209.s:
tadudbhavāni patrāṇi gṛhītvā surasattamāḥ ..
apūrvāṇi sugaṃdhīni matvā te bhakṣayaṃti ca .. 51 ..
5.209.d:
तदुद्भवानि पत्राणि गृहीत्वा सुरसत्तमाः ..
अपूर्वाणि सुगंधीनि मत्वा ते भक्षयंति च .. 51 ..
5.209.m: Taking the leaves born from it, the foremost gods / ate them, considering them extraordinary and fragrant. 51.

5.209.s: vaktraśuddhikṛte rājanviśeṣeṇa praharṣitāḥ .. 52 ..
5.209.d: वक्त्रशुद्धिकृते राजन्विशेषेण प्रहर्षिताः .. 52 ..
5.209.m: They were especially delighted, O King, for the purpose of purifying their mouths. 52.

5.209.s:
atha dhanvatarirvaidyaḥ svabuddhyā pṛthivīpate ..
nāgālāne yato jātā nāgavallī bhaviṣyati .. 53 ..
5.209.d:
अथ धन्वतरिर्वैद्यः स्वबुद्ध्या पृथिवीपते ..
नागालाने यतो जाता नागवल्ली भविष्यति .. 53 ..
5.209.m: Then the physician Dhanvantari, through his own discernment, O lord of the earth, [reflected]: / 'Since it grew at the tethering-post of an elephant (nāga), it shall be the nāgavallī (betel-vine). 53.

5.209.s:
sadā smarasya saṃsthānaṃ mama vākyādbhaviṣyati ..
nāgavallīti vai nāma tasyāścakre tataḥ param .. 54 ..
5.209.d:
सदा स्मरस्य संस्थानं मम वाक्याद्भविष्यति ..
नागवल्लीति वै नाम तस्याश्चक्रे ततः परम् .. 54 ..
5.209.m: By my word, it shall forever be the abode of Smara.' / Thereafter he gave it the name nāgavallī. 54.

5.209.s:
saṃyogaṃ ca cakārātha tāṃbūlaṃ jāyate yathā ..
pūgīphalena cūrṇena khadireṇāpi pārthiva .. 55 ..
5.209.d:
संयोगं च चकाराथ तांबूलं जायते यथा ..
पूगीफलेन चूर्णेन खदिरेणापि पार्थिव .. 55 ..
5.209.m: And he made the combination so that betel (tāmbūla) is produced / with areca nut, lime, and catechu, O earthly king. 55.

5.209.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya vāṇīvatsarako nṛpaḥ ..
pratoṣaṃ nītavāñchakraṃ tapasā nirmalena ca .. 56 ..
5.209.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य वाणीवत्सरको नृपः ..
प्रतोषं नीतवाञ्छक्रं तपसा निर्मलेन च .. 56 ..
5.209.m: After some time, King Vāṇīvatsaraka / pleased Śakra with stainless austerity. 56.

5.209.s: tatastattapasā tuṣṭa indro vacanamabravīt .. 57 ..
5.209.d: ततस्तत्तपसा तुष्ट इन्द्रो वचनमब्रवीत् .. 57 ..
5.209.m: Pleased with that austerity, Indra then spoke these words: 57.

5.209.s:
.. indra uvāca .. ..
bhobhoḥ pārthiva tuṣṭo'smi tapasā'nena sāṃpratam ..
brūhi yatte varaṃ dadmi manasā vāṃchitaṃ sadā .. 58 ..
5.209.d:
.. इन्द्र उवाच .. ..
भोभोः पार्थिव तुष्टोऽस्मि तपसाऽनेन सांप्रतम् ..
ब्रूहि यत्ते वरं दद्मि मनसा वांछितं सदा .. 58 ..
5.209.m: Indra said: / 'O earthly king, I am now pleased with this austerity. / Speak, that I may grant you the boon that your heart has always desired.' 58.

5.209.s:
so'bravīdyadi me tuṣṭo yadi deyo varo mama ..
vimānaṃ khecaraṃ dehi yenāgacchāmi te gṛhe ..
nityameva dharāpṛṣṭhādvaṃdanārthaṃ tava prabho ..59..
5.209.d:
सोऽब्रवीद्यदि मे तुष्टो यदि देयो वरो मम ..
विमानं खेचरं देहि येनागच्छामि ते गृहे ..
नित्यमेव धरापृष्ठाद्वंदनार्थं तव प्रभो ..59..
5.209.m: He said: 'If you are pleased with me, if a boon is to be given to me, / grant me an aerial chariot traveling through the sky, by which I may come to your home / continually from the surface of the earth to pay homage to you, O Lord.' 59.

5.209.s:
sa tatheti pratijñāya haṃsabarhiṇanāditam ..
vimānaṃ pradadau tasmai manomārutavegadhṛk .. 6.210.60 ..
5.209.d:
स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय हंसबर्हिणनादितम् ..
विमानं प्रददौ तस्मै मनोमारुतवेगधृक् .. 6.210.60 ..
5.209.m: Agreeing with 'So be it,' he gave him an aerial chariot / resounding with the calls of swans and peacocks, possessing the speed of mind and wind. 60.

5.209.s:
sa tatra nityamāruhya prayāti tridaśālayam ..
bhaktyā paramayā yuktaḥ sahasrākṣaṃ pravaṃditum .. 61 ..
5.209.d:
स तत्र नित्यमारुह्य प्रयाति त्रिदशालयम् ..
भक्त्या परमया युक्तः सहस्राक्षं प्रवंदितुम् .. 61 ..
5.209.m: Ascending it daily, he went to the abode of the thirty [gods] / filled with supreme devotion, to salute the thousand-eyed [Indra]. 61.

5.209.s:
tasya śakraḥ svahastena tāṃbūlaṃ ca prayacchati ..
sa ca tadbhakṣayāmāsa prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā .. 62 ..
5.209.d:
तस्य शक्रः स्वहस्तेन तांबूलं च प्रयच्छति ..
स च तद्भक्षयामास प्रहृष्टेनांतरात्मना .. 62 ..
5.209.m: Śakra gave him betel with his own hand, / and he chewed it with a delighted heart. 62.

5.209.s:
vṛddhabhāve'pi saṃprāpte tasya kāmo'tyavarddhata ..
tāṃbūlasya prabhāvena sumahānpṛthivīpate .. 63 ..
5.209.d:
वृद्धभावेऽपि संप्राप्ते तस्य कामोऽत्यवर्द्धत ..
तांबूलस्य प्रभावेन सुमहान्पृथिवीपते .. 63 ..
5.209.m: Even when old age arrived, his desire increased exceedingly / by the power of the betel, O lord of the earth, becoming very great. 63.

5.209.s:
atha śakramuvācedaṃ sa rājā vinayānvitaḥ ..
nāgavallīpradānena prasādo me vidhīyatām .. 64 ..
5.209.d:
अथ शक्रमुवाचेदं स राजा विनयान्वितः ..
नागवल्लीप्रदानेन प्रसादो मे विधीयताम् .. 64 ..
5.209.m: Then, endowed with humility, that king said to Śakra: / 'Let favor be shown to me by the gift of the nāgavallī, 64.

5.209.s:
martyaloke samānetuṃ pracāraṃ yena gacchati ..
sa tatheti pratijñāya tasmai tāṃ pradadau tadā .. 65 ..
5.209.d:
मर्त्यलोके समानेतुं प्रचारं येन गच्छति ..
स तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय तस्मै तां प्रददौ तदा .. 65 ..
5.209.m: so that it may be brought to the mortal world and come into widespread use.' / Agreeing with 'So be it,' he then gave it to him. 65.

5.209.s:
gatvā nijapuraṃ sopi svodyāne'sthāpayattadā ..
tataḥ kālena mahatā pracāraṃ sā gatā kṣitau .. 66 ..
5.209.d:
गत्वा निजपुरं सोपि स्वोद्यानेऽस्थापयत्तदा ..
ततः कालेन महता प्रचारं सा गता क्षितौ .. 66 ..
5.209.m: Having returned to his city, he also planted it in his garden; / then, in the course of much time, it spread throughout the earth. 66.

5.209.s:
yasyāḥ svādanato lokaḥ kāmātmā samapadyata ..
na kaścidyajanaṃ cakre yājanaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ ..
anyā dharmakriyāḥ sarvāḥ praṇaṣṭā dharmasaṃbhavāḥ .. 67 ..
5.209.d:
यस्याः स्वादनतो लोकः कामात्मा समपद्यत ..
न कश्चिद्यजनं चक्रे याजनं च विशेषतः ..
अन्या धर्मक्रियाः सर्वाः प्रणष्टा धर्मसंभवाः .. 67 ..
5.209.m: From tasting it, people became lustful; / no one performed sacrifices, especially not officiating for others; / all other righteous actions born of dharma were destroyed. 67.

5.209.s:
tato devagaṇāḥ sarve yajñabhāgavivarjitāḥ ..
pīḍyamānāḥ krudhā viṣṭā gatvā procuḥ pitāmaham .. 68 ..
5.209.d:
ततो देवगणाः सर्वे यज्ञभागविवर्जिताः ..
पीड्यमानाः क्रुधा विष्टा गत्वा प्रोचुः पितामहम् .. 68 ..
5.209.m: Then all the hosts of gods, deprived of their sacrificial shares, / tormented and overcome with anger, went and spoke to the Grandfather: 68.

5.209.s:
martyaloke suraśreṣṭha naṣṭā dharmakriyā bhṛśam ..
kāmāsakto yato lokastāṃbūlasya ca bhakṣaṇāt ..
tasmātkuru prasādaṃ no yenāsmākaṃ kriyā bhavet .. 69 ..
5.209.d:
मर्त्यलोके सुरश्रेष्ठ नष्टा धर्मक्रिया भृशम् ..
कामासक्तो यतो लोकस्तांबूलस्य च भक्षणात् ..
तस्मात्कुरु प्रसादं नो येनास्माकं क्रिया भवेत् .. 69 ..
5.209.m: 'O best of gods, righteous actions in the mortal world are utterly destroyed, / because people are devoted to lust from consuming betel. / Therefore, grant us favor so that our rites may be performed.' 69.

5.209.s:
etasminneva kāle tu puṣkarasthaṃ pitāmaham ..
yajanārthe samāyātaṃ daridro vīkṣya pārthiva .. 6.210.70 ..
5.209.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु पुष्करस्थं पितामहम् ..
यजनार्थे समायातं दरिद्रो वीक्ष्य पार्थिव .. 6.210.70 ..
5.209.m: At that very time, seeing the Grandfather residing at Puṣkara, / who had arrived for the purpose of a sacrifice, O earthly king, a poor man (Daridra), 70.

5.209.s:
praṇipatya tataḥ prāha vinayāvanataḥ sthitaḥ ..
nirviṇṇo'haṃ suraśreṣṭha brāhmaṇānāṃ gṛhe sthitaḥ .. 71 ..
5.209.d:
प्रणिपत्य ततः प्राह विनयावनतः स्थितः ..
निर्विण्णोऽहं सुरश्रेष्ठ ब्राह्मणानां गृहे स्थितः .. 71 ..
5.209.m: bowed down and, standing bent with humility, said: / 'O best of gods, I am dejected, dwelling in the houses of brahmins. 71.

5.209.s:
tasmātkīrtaya me sthānaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ vittavatāṃ hi yat ..
tatra sañjāyate tṛptiḥ śāśvatī pracurā prabho .. 72 ..
5.209.d:
तस्मात्कीर्तय मे स्थानं श्रेष्ठं वित्तवतां हि यत् ..
तत्र सञ्जायते तृप्तिः शाश्वती प्रचुरा प्रभो .. 72 ..
5.209.m: Therefore, declare to me an excellent place that belongs to the wealthy; / there lasting and abundant satisfaction arises, O Lord.' 72.

5.209.s:
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā ciraṃ dhyātvā pitāmahaḥ ..
abravīcca daridraṃ taṃ chidrārthaṃ dhaninā miha .. 73 ..
5.209.d:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा चिरं ध्यात्वा पितामहः ..
अब्रवीच्च दरिद्रं तं छिद्रार्थं धनिना मिह .. 73 ..
5.209.m: Hearing his words and meditating for a long time, the Grandfather / spoke to that Daridra regarding vulnerabilities for the wealthy in this world: 73.

5.209.s:
cūrṇapatre tvayā vāsaḥ sadā kāryo daridra bhoḥ ..
tāṃbūlasya tu parṇāgre bhāryayā mama vākyataḥ .. 74 ..
5.209.d:
चूर्णपत्रे त्वया वासः सदा कार्यो दरिद्र भोः ..
तांबूलस्य तु पर्णाग्रे भार्यया मम वाक्यतः .. 74 ..
5.209.m: 'O Daridra, you must always reside in the vessel of lime, / and by my word, your wife [must dwell] at the tip of the betel leaf. 74.

5.209.s:
parṇānāṃ caiva vṛṃteṣu sarveṣu tvatsutena ca ..
rātrau khadirasāre ca tvaṃ tābhyāṃ sarvadā vasa .. 75 ..
5.209.d:
पर्णानां चैव वृंतेषु सर्वेषु त्वत्सुतेन च ..
रात्रौ खदिरसारे च त्वं ताभ्यां सर्वदा वस .. 75 ..
5.209.m: Your son must dwell on the stalks of all the leaves; / and at night you, along with the two of them, must always reside in the catechu. 75.

5.209.s:
dhanināṃ chidrakṛtproktametatsthānacatuṣṭayam ..
pārthivānāṃ viśeṣeṇa mama vākyā dvraja drutam .. 76 ..
5.209.d:
धनिनां छिद्रकृत्प्रोक्तमेतत्स्थानचतुष्टयम् ..
पार्थिवानां विशेषेण मम वाक्या द्व्रज द्रुतम् .. 76 ..
5.209.m: This group of four places is declared to cause vulnerability to the wealthy, / especially to kings; go swiftly at my command.' 76.

5.209.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ yatpṛṣṭo'smi narādhipa .. 77 ..
5.209.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं यत्पृष्टोऽस्मि नराधिप .. 77 ..
5.209.m: Nārada said: / 'All this has been related to you, as I was asked, O lord of men. 77.

5.209.s:
tāṃbūlotthāni chidrāṇi yathā syurdhanināmiha ..
tāni sarvāṇi cīrṇāni tvayā rājannajānatā ..
tena vai vibhavocchittiḥ saṃjātā sahasā nṛpa .. 78 ..
5.209.d:
तांबूलोत्थानि छिद्राणि यथा स्युर्धनिनामिह ..
तानि सर्वाणि चीर्णानि त्वया राजन्नजानता ..
तेन वै विभवोच्छित्तिः संजाता सहसा नृप .. 78 ..
5.209.m: The vulnerabilities arising from betel that befall the wealthy here— / all of those have been committed by you without knowing, O King; / therefore indeed your wealth was suddenly destroyed, O King.' 78.

5.209.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
tadarthamapi me brūhi prāyaścittaṃ munīśvara ..
kadācidbhakṣaṇaṃ me syāttāṃbūlasya tathāvidham .. 79 ..
5.209.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
तदर्थमपि मे ब्रूहि प्रायश्चित्तं मुनीश्वर ..
कदाचिद्भक्षणं मे स्यात्तांबूलस्य तथाविधम् .. 79 ..
5.209.m: The king said: / For that reason also, tell me the expiation, O lord among sages, / should I ever eat betel in such an [improper] manner,

5.209.s: yena sañjāyate śuddhiḥ kutāṃbūlasamudbhavā .. 6.210.80 ..
5.209.d: येन सञ्जायते शुद्धिः कुतांबूलसमुद्भवा .. 6.210.80 ..
5.209.m: by which purification arises from bad betel.

5.209.s:
.. viśvā mitra uvāca .. ..
śṛṇu rājanpravakṣyāmi prāyaścittaṃ tu yaccaret ..
āśvāsanena śuddhyarthaṃ kutāṃbūlasya bhakṣaṇāt .. 81 ..
5.209.d:
.. विश्वा मित्र उवाच .. ..
शृणु राजन्प्रवक्ष्यामि प्रायश्चित्तं तु यच्चरेत् ..
आश्वासनेन शुद्ध्यर्थं कुतांबूलस्य भक्षणात् .. 81 ..
5.209.m: Viśvāmitra said: / Listen, O king, I will tell the expiation that one should perform / for the sake of purification and reassurance after the eating of bad betel.

5.209.s:
parvakālaṃ samuddiśya samyakchraddhāsamanvitaḥ ..
ānayedbrāhmaṇaṃ rājanvedavedāṃgapāragam .. 82 ..
5.209.d:
पर्वकालं समुद्दिश्य सम्यक्छ्रद्धासमन्वितः ..
आनयेद्ब्राह्मणं राजन्वेदवेदांगपारगम् .. 82 ..
5.209.m: Focusing upon an auspicious occasion and full of proper faith, / one should bring a brahmin, O king, who has mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas.

5.209.s:
prakṣālya caraṇau tasya vāsasī paridhāpayet ..
saṃpūjya gaṃdhapuṣpādyaistataḥ patraṃ hiraṇmayam ..
svaśaktyā kārayitvā'tha cūrṇe muktāphalaṃ nyaset .. 83 ..
5.209.d:
प्रक्षाल्य चरणौ तस्य वाससी परिधापयेत् ..
संपूज्य गंधपुष्पाद्यैस्ततः पत्रं हिरण्मयम् ..
स्वशक्त्या कारयित्वाऽथ चूर्णे मुक्ताफलं न्यसेत् .. 83 ..
5.209.m: Having washed his feet, one should clothe him in two garments; / having worshipped him with fragrant pastes, flowers, and the like, then having had a gold leaf made / according to one's means, one should place a pearl on the lime,

5.209.s:
pūgīphalaṃ ca vaiḍūryaṃ khadiraṃ rūpyameva ca ..
mantreṇānena viprāya tathaiva ca samarpayet .. 84 ..
5.209.d:
पूगीफलं च वैडूर्यं खदिरं रूप्यमेव च ..
मन्त्रेणानेन विप्राय तथैव च समर्पयेत् .. 84 ..
5.209.m: and lapis lazuli for the areca nut, and silver indeed for the catechu; / and by this mantra one should offer it likewise to the brahmin:

5.209.s:
yanmayā bhakṣitaṃ pūrvaṃ vṛntaṃ patrasamudbhavam..
cūrṇapatraṃ tathaivānyadrātrau khadirameva ca .. 85 ..
5.209.d:
यन्मया भक्षितं पूर्वं वृन्तं पत्रसमुद्भवम्..
चूर्णपत्रं तथैवान्यद्रात्रौ खदिरमेव च .. 85 ..
5.209.m: "Whatever stalk belonging to a leaf was eaten by me before, / or a leaf with lime, or likewise other catechu at night—

5.209.s:
tasya pāpasya śuddhyarthaṃ tāṃbūlaṃ pratigṛhyatām ..
tatastu brāhmaṇo maṃtramevaṃ rājannudāharet .. 86 ..
5.209.d:
तस्य पापस्य शुद्ध्यर्थं तांबूलं प्रतिगृह्यताम् ..
ततस्तु ब्राह्मणो मंत्रमेवं राजन्नुदाहरेत् .. 86 ..
5.209.m: for the purification of that sin, let this betel be accepted." / Then the brahmin should utter the mantra thus, O king:

5.209.s:
yajamānahitārthāya sarvapāpaviśuddhaye ..
ajñānājjñānato vāpi kutāṃbūlaṃ prabhakṣitam .. 87 ..
5.209.d:
यजमानहितार्थाय सर्वपापविशुद्धये ..
अज्ञानाज्ज्ञानतो वापि कुतांबूलं प्रभक्षितम् .. 87 ..
5.209.m: "For the benefit of the patron and for the complete purification of all sins, / whatever bad betel was eaten, through ignorance or even knowingly,

5.209.s:
bhakṣayiṣyasi yaccānyatkadācinme prasādanāt ..
tasya doṣo na te bhāvī mama vākyādasaṃśayam .. 88 ..
5.209.d:
भक्षयिष्यसि यच्चान्यत्कदाचिन्मे प्रसादनात् ..
तस्य दोषो न ते भावी मम वाक्यादसंशयम् .. 88 ..
5.209.m: and whatever else you may eat at some time through my favor, / no fault of that shall belong to you, beyond doubt, according to my word."

5.209.s:
anena vidhinā dattvā tāṃbūlaṃ śuddhimāpnuyāt ..
kutāṃbūlasya doṣeṇa gṛhyate na naro nṛpa .. 89 ..
5.209.d:
अनेन विधिना दत्त्वा तांबूलं शुद्धिमाप्नुयात् ..
कुतांबूलस्य दोषेण गृह्यते न नरो नृप .. 89 ..
5.209.m: Having given betel according to this rule, one attains purification; / a man is not seized by the fault of bad betel, O king.

5.209.s:
tasmāttvaṃ hi mahārāja vratametatsamācara ..
bahu puṇyatamaṃ hyetanmahābhogavivarddhanam .. 6.210.90 ..
5.209.d:
तस्मात्त्वं हि महाराज व्रतमेतत्समाचर ..
बहु पुण्यतमं ह्येतन्महाभोगविवर्द्धनम् .. 6.210.90 ..
5.209.m: Therefore, O great king, perform this rite; / for this is most meritorious and increases great enjoyment.

5.209.s:
yaḥ prayacchati rājendra vidhinānena bhaktitaḥ ..
janmajanmāntare vāpi na tāṃbūlena mucyate .. 91 ..
5.209.d:
यः प्रयच्छति राजेन्द्र विधिनानेन भक्तितः ..
जन्मजन्मान्तरे वापि न तांबूलेन मुच्यते .. 91 ..
5.209.m: Whoever gives [it] according to this rule with devotion, O lord of kings, / is never deprived of betel, even in another birth.

5.209.s:
tāṃbūlaṃ bhakṣayitvā yo naitaddānaṃ prayacchati ..
tāṃbūlavarjitaḥ so'tra bhavejjanmanijanmani .. 92 ..
5.209.d:
तांबूलं भक्षयित्वा यो नैतद्दानं प्रयच्छति ..
तांबूलवर्जितः सोऽत्र भवेज्जन्मनिजन्मनि .. 92 ..
5.209.m: Whoever, having eaten betel, does not give this gift, / would become devoid of betel here birth after birth.

5.209.s:
tāṃbūlavarjitaṃ yasya mukhaṃ syātpṛthivīpate ..
kṛpaṇasya daridrasya tadbilaṃ na hi tanmukham .. 93 ..
5.209.d:
तांबूलवर्जितं यस्य मुखं स्यात्पृथिवीपते ..
कृपणस्य दरिद्रस्य तद्बिलं न हि तन्मुखम् .. 93 ..
5.209.m: The mouth of a wretched, impoverished man that is devoid of betel, / O lord of the earth, is a hole, not a mouth!

5.209.s:
tāṃbūlaṃ brāhmaṇendrāya yo dattvā prākprabhakṣayet ..
surūpo bhāgyavāndakṣo bhavejjanmanijanmani .. 94 ..
5.209.d:
तांबूलं ब्राह्मणेन्द्राय यो दत्त्वा प्राक्प्रभक्षयेत् ..
सुरूपो भाग्यवान्दक्षो भवेज्जन्मनिजन्मनि .. 94 ..
5.209.m: Whoever gives betel to an eminent brahmin before eating [it himself], / becomes handsome, fortunate, and capable birth after birth.

5.209.s:
etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ kutāṃbūlasya bhakṣaṇāt ..
yatphalaṃ jāyate puṃsāṃ yaddānena mahīpate .. 95 ..
5.209.d:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं कुतांबूलस्य भक्षणात् ..
यत्फलं जायते पुंसां यद्दानेन महीपते .. 95 ..
5.209.m: All this has been told to you: what fruit arises for men / from eating bad betel, and what [arises] through this gift, O lord of the earth,

5.209.s:
śaṃkhādityānuṣaṃgeṇa tāṃbūlasya ca bhakṣaṇe ..
ye doṣā ye guṇā rājandānaṃ caiva prabhakṣaṇe .. 96 ..
5.209.d:
शंखादित्यानुषंगेण तांबूलस्य च भक्षणे ..
ये दोषा ये गुणा राजन्दानं चैव प्रभक्षणे .. 96 ..
5.209.m: in connection with Śaṅkhāditya, and in the eating of betel, / which faults and which virtues there are, O king, and the gift itself at the time of eating.

5.209.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye tāṃbūlotpatti tāṃbūlamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma daśottaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 210 .. .. .. ..
5.209.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये तांबूलोत्पत्ति तांबूलमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम दशोत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः .. 210 .. .. .. ..
5.209.m: Thus ends the two hundred and tenth chapter, entitled "Description of the Origin of Betel and the Betel-māhātmya", in the Hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmya of the sixth section, the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.210.s:
.. viśvāmitra uvāca .. ..
rājño dāridryadoṣasya kuṣṭhavyādheśca kāraṇam ..
kathayitvā punaḥ prāha nārado munisattamaḥ .. 1 ..
5.210.d:
.. विश्वामित्र उवाच .. ..
राज्ञो दारिद्र्यदोषस्य कुष्ठव्याधेश्च कारणम् ..
कथयित्वा पुनः प्राह नारदो मुनिसत्तमः .. 1 ..
5.210.m: Viśvāmitra said: / Having explained the cause of the king's poverty and leprosy, / Nārada, the best of sages, spoke again.

5.210.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ rājankuṣṭhasya kāraṇam ..
dāridryasya ca yatsamyagjñātvā divyena cakṣuṣā .. 2 ..
5.210.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं राजन्कुष्ठस्य कारणम् ..
दारिद्र्यस्य च यत्सम्यग्ज्ञात्वा दिव्येन चक्षुषा .. 2 ..
5.210.m: Nārada said: / All this has been told to you, O king, the cause of leprosy / and of poverty, which I knew correctly with my divine eye.

5.210.s:
adhunā saṃpravakṣyāmi yathā tava parābhavaḥ ..
śatrubhyaḥ saṃprajāto'tra dvijānāmapamānataḥ .. 3 ..
5.210.d:
अधुना संप्रवक्ष्यामि यथा तव पराभवः ..
शत्रुभ्यः संप्रजातोऽत्र द्विजानामपमानतः .. 3 ..
5.210.m: Now I will explain how your defeat / at the hands of your enemies arose here from the disrespect shown to brahmins.

5.210.s:
ānartādhipatiryo'tra kaścidrājye'bhiṣicyate ..
sa pūrvaṃ gacchati grāmaṃ nāgarāṇāṃ prabhaktitaḥ .. 4 ..
5.210.d:
आनर्ताधिपतिर्योऽत्र कश्चिद्राज्येऽभिषिच्यते ..
स पूर्वं गच्छति ग्रामं नागराणां प्रभक्तितः .. 4 ..
5.210.m: Whoever is consecrated in the kingship here as the lord of Ānarta, / goes first to the village of the Nāgaras with great devotion.

5.210.s:
tvayā tatkalpitaṃ rājannaiva dattaṃ pramādataḥ ..
parābhūtā dvijāste ca yācamānā muhurmuhuḥ .. 5 ..
5.210.d:
त्वया तत्कल्पितं राजन्नैव दत्तं प्रमादतः ..
पराभूता द्विजास्ते च याचमाना मुहुर्मुहुः .. 5 ..
5.210.m: What was assigned for them, O king, was not given by you through negligence; / and those twice-born, begging repeatedly, were turned away.

5.210.s:
tathā kopavaśādyāni śāsanāni dvijanmanām ..
lopitāni tvayānyāni pitṛpaitāmahāni ca .. 6 ..
5.210.d:
तथा कोपवशाद्यानि शासनानि द्विजन्मनाम् ..
लोपितानि त्वयान्यानि पितृपैतामहानि च .. 6 ..
5.210.m: Likewise, under the influence of anger, other land-grants belonging to the twice-born / that had descended from your fathers and grandfathers were revoked by you.

5.210.s:
tena te'tra parābhūtiḥ saṃjātā śatrusaṃbhavā ..
evaṃ jñātvā dvijedrāṇāṃ śāsa nāni prayaccha bhoḥ .. 7 ..
5.210.d:
तेन तेऽत्र पराभूतिः संजाता शत्रुसंभवा ..
एवं ज्ञात्वा द्विजेद्राणां शास नानि प्रयच्छ भोः .. 7 ..
5.210.m: Because of that, your defeat by enemies occurred here. / Knowing this, grant royal charters to the lords among the twice-born, O king!

5.210.s:
gṛhītāni ca yānyeva teṣāṃ mokṣaṃ samācara ..
tacchrutvā pārthivaḥ so'tha śaṃkhatīrthe prabhaktitaḥ .. 8 ..
5.210.d:
गृहीतानि च यान्येव तेषां मोक्षं समाचर ..
तच्छ्रुत्वा पार्थिवः सोऽथ शंखतीर्थे प्रभक्तितः .. 8 ..
5.210.m: And release those [lands] which were seized! / Hearing that, that king then with great devotion at Śaṅkhatīrtha,

5.210.s:
snātvā viprānsamā hūya madhyagena samanvitān ..
śaṃkhādityasya purataḥ prakṣālya caraṇau nṛpa .. 9 ..
5.210.d:
स्नात्वा विप्रान्समा हूय मध्यगेन समन्वितान् ..
शंखादित्यस्य पुरतः प्रक्षाल्य चरणौ नृप .. 9 ..
5.210.m: having bathed and summoned the brahmins together with their intermediary, / and having washed their feet before Śaṅkhāditya, O king,

5.210.s:
dadau ca śāsanaśataṃ prakṣālya caraṇāṃstataḥ ..
ṣaḍviṃśatyadhikaṃ rājā nāgarāṇāṃ mahātmanām .. 6.211.10 ..
5.210.d:
ददौ च शासनशतं प्रक्षाल्य चरणांस्ततः ..
षड्विंशत्यधिकं राजा नागराणां महात्मनाम् .. 6.211.10 ..
5.210.m: the king, having washed their feet, gave a hundred / and twenty-six charters to the noble Nāgaras.

5.210.s:
etasminnaṃtare tatra śatravo ye ca saṃsthitāḥ ..
sarve mṛtyuṃ samāpannā brāhmaṇānāṃ prasādataḥ .. 11 ..
5.210.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे तत्र शत्रवो ये च संस्थिताः ..
सर्वे मृत्युं समापन्ना ब्राह्मणानां प्रसादतः .. 11 ..
5.210.m: In the meantime, the enemies who were established there / all met their death through the grace of the brahmins.

5.210.s:
viśvāmitra uvāca .. ..
etatte sarvamākhyātaṃ śaṃkhatīrthasamudbhavam ..
prabhāvaṃ pārthivaśreṣṭha kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi .. 12 ..
5.210.d:
विश्वामित्र उवाच .. ..
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं शंखतीर्थसमुद्भवम् ..
प्रभावं पार्थिवश्रेष्ठ किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि .. 12 ..
5.210.m: Viśvāmitra said: / All this power arising from Śaṅkhatīrtha has been told to you, / O best of kings. What more do you wish to hear?

5.210.s: iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye śaṃkhatīrthamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmaikādaśottaradviśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ ..211..
5.210.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये शंखतीर्थमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनामैकादशोत्तरद्विशततमोऽध्यायः ..211..
5.210.m: Thus ends the two hundred and eleventh chapter, entitled "Description of the Śaṅkhatīrthamāhātmya", in the Hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmya of the sixth section, the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses.

5.211.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
śrutaṃ tīrthatrayaṃ puṇyaṃ hāṭakeśvarasaṃjñite ..
kṣetre'tra yattvayā proktamasmākaṃ sūtanaṃdana .. 1 ..
5.211.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
श्रुतं तीर्थत्रयं पुण्यं हाटकेश्वरसंज्ञिते ..
क्षेत्रेऽत्र यत्त्वया प्रोक्तमस्माकं सूतनंदन .. 1 ..
5.211.m: The seers said: / The holy triad of sacred fords has been heard in this sacred field / called Hāṭakeśvara, which was described by you to us, O son of Sūta.

5.211.s:
viśvāmitrīyamāhātmyaṃ śrotumicchāmahe vayam..
sāṃprataṃ tatsamācakṣva paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ .. 2 ..
5.211.d:
विश्वामित्रीयमाहात्म्यं श्रोतुमिच्छामहे वयम्..
सांप्रतं तत्समाचक्ष्व परं कौतूहलं हि नः .. 2 ..
5.211.m: We wish to hear the māhātmya belonging to Viśvāmitra; / explain that to us now, for our curiosity is immense.

5.211.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
samudrasyāpi pāro'tra lakṣyate ca kṣiterapi ..
tārakāṇāṃ munestasya na guṇānāṃ dvijottamāḥ .. 3 ..
5.211.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
समुद्रस्यापि पारोऽत्र लक्ष्यते च क्षितेरपि ..
तारकाणां मुनेस्तस्य न गुणानां द्विजोत्तमाः .. 3 ..
5.211.m: Sūta said: / The other shore of the ocean and of the earth can be discerned here, / as can the stars, O best of the twice-born, but of that sage's virtues,

5.211.s:
lakṣyate kenacitpāro gādheḥ putrasya dhīmataḥ ..
kṣatriyo'pi dvijatvaṃ yaḥ saṃprāpto dvijasattamāḥ.. .. 4
5.211.d:
लक्ष्यते केनचित्पारो गाधेः पुत्रस्य धीमतः ..
क्षत्रियोऽपि द्विजत्वं यः संप्राप्तो द्विजसत्तमाः.. .. 4
5.211.m: the limit cannot be discerned by anyone, of that wise son of Gādhi, / who, though a kṣatriya, attained the status of a brahmin, O best of the twice-born;

5.211.s:
aṃtyajatvaṃ gatasyāpi triśaṃkoḥ pṛthivīpateḥ ..
yajñabhāgabhujo devāḥ pratyakṣeṇa vinirmitāḥ .. 5 ..
5.211.d:
अंत्यजत्वं गतस्यापि त्रिशंकोः पृथिवीपतेः ..
यज्ञभागभुजो देवाः प्रत्यक्षेण विनिर्मिताः .. 5 ..
5.211.m: by whom, even when King Triśaṅku had fallen to the state of an outcaste, / the gods were visibly made to partake of sacrificial shares;

5.211.s:
brahmaṇaḥ spardhayā yena purā sṛṣṭirdvijottamāḥ ..
prārabdhā ca tato devaiḥ praṇipatya nivāritaḥ .. 6 ..
5.211.d:
ब्रह्मणः स्पर्धया येन पुरा सृष्टिर्द्विजोत्तमाः ..
प्रारब्धा च ततो देवैः प्रणिपत्य निवारितः .. 6 ..
5.211.m: by whom, in rivalry with Brahmā of old, O best of the twice-born, a creation / was commenced, and then he was dissuaded by the gods who bowed down [to him].

5.211.s:
tasya tīrthasya māhātmyaṃ sāprataṃ vadato mama ..
śrūyatāṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhāḥ sarvapātakanāśa nam .. 7 ..
5.211.d:
तस्य तीर्थस्य माहात्म्यं साप्रतं वदतो मम ..
श्रूयतां ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठाः सर्वपातकनाश नम् .. 7 ..
5.211.m: Let the māhātmya of his sacred ford, which destroys all sins, / be heard from me as I speak [of it] now, O best of brahmins.

5.211.s:
tena tatra kṛtaṃ kuṇḍaṃ svahastena mahātmanā ..
śastraṃ vināpi bhūpṛṣṭhaṃ pravidārya samaṃtataḥ .. 8 ..
5.211.d:
तेन तत्र कृतं कुण्डं स्वहस्तेन महात्मना ..
शस्त्रं विनापि भूपृष्ठं प्रविदार्य समंततः .. 8 ..
5.211.m: By him, that noble soul, a pool was made there with his own hand, / tearing open the earth's surface on all sides even without a weapon.

5.211.s:
tatra dhyātvā samānītā pātālājjāhnavī nadī ..
martyaloke samāyātaṃ yasyāstoyaṃ sunirmalam .. 9 ..
5.211.d:
तत्र ध्यात्वा समानीता पातालाज्जाह्नवी नदी ..
मर्त्यलोके समायातं यस्यास्तोयं सुनिर्मलम् .. 9 ..
5.211.m: There, having meditated, the river Jāhnavī was brought from Pātāla, / whose very pure water came forth into the mortal world.

5.211.s:
susvādu ca tathā snānātsarvapātakanāśanam ..
tenāpi sthāpitastatra bhāskaro vāritaskaraḥ .. 6.212.10 ..
5.211.d:
सुस्वादु च तथा स्नानात्सर्वपातकनाशनम् ..
तेनापि स्थापितस्तत्र भास्करो वारितस्करः .. 6.212.10 ..
5.211.m: and very sweet, destroying all sins through ritual ablution. / By him too the Sun, the remover of darkness, was established there.

5.211.s:
yaḥ saptamyāṃ sūryavāre snātvā tasya hṛde śubhe ..
māghamāse site pakṣe namasyati divākaram ..
sa kuṣṭhairmucyate sarvaistathā pāpairdvijo ttamāḥ .. 11 ..
5.211.d:
यः सप्तम्यां सूर्यवारे स्नात्वा तस्य हृदे शुभे ..
माघमासे सिते पक्षे नमस्यति दिवाकरम् ..
स कुष्ठैर्मुच्यते सर्वैस्तथा पापैर्द्विजो त्तमाः .. 11 ..
5.211.m: Whoever, having bathed in his auspicious pool on a Sunday that is a seventh lunar day / in the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha, bows to the Sun, / is freed from all leprosy as well as sins, O best of brahmins.

5.211.s:
paścimottaradigbhāge tasyāsti jalasaṃbhavā ..
dhanvaṃtarikṛtā vāpī sarvarogavināśinī .. 12 ..
5.211.d:
पश्चिमोत्तरदिग्भागे तस्यास्ति जलसंभवा ..
धन्वंतरिकृता वापी सर्वरोगविनाशिनी .. 12 ..
5.211.m: In the northwestern quarter from it, there is a step-well produced from water, / constructed by Dhanvantari, which destroys all diseases.

5.211.s:
tatra pūrvaṃ tapastepe dhanvaṃ tarirudāradhīḥ ..
vavande tapasā yukto dhyāyamānaḥ samāhitaḥ .. 13 ..
5.211.d:
तत्र पूर्वं तपस्तेपे धन्वं तरिरुदारधीः ..
ववन्दे तपसा युक्तो ध्यायमानः समाहितः .. 13 ..
5.211.m: There previously Dhanvantari of noble intellect performed austerity; / endowed with austerity, meditating and composed, he offered praise.

5.211.s:
tataḥ kālena mahatā saṃtuṣṭastasya bhāskaraḥ ..
uvāca varado'smīti prārthayasva mahāmate .. 14 ..
5.211.d:
ततः कालेन महता संतुष्टस्तस्य भास्करः ..
उवाच वरदोऽस्मीति प्रार्थयस्व महामते .. 14 ..
5.211.m: Then after a long time the Sun, pleased with him, / said: “I am a giver of boons; ask [a boon], O noble-minded one.”

5.211.s:
.. dhanvaṃtariruvāca .. ..
atra kuṇḍe naro bhaktyā yaḥ snānaṃ kurute vibho ..
tasya syātsarvarogāṇāṃ saṃkṣayaḥ surasattama .. 15 ..
5.211.d:
.. धन्वंतरिरुवाच .. ..
अत्र कुण्डे नरो भक्त्या यः स्नानं कुरुते विभो ..
तस्य स्यात्सर्वरोगाणां संक्षयः सुरसत्तम .. 15 ..
5.211.m: Dhanvantari said: / “The person who with devotion performs ritual ablution in this pool, O lord, / for him may there be the destruction of all diseases, O best of gods.”

5.211.s:
.. śrībhagavānuvāca .. ..
adya śaste dine yo'tra saptamyāṃ ravivāsare ..
sūryodaye naraḥ snānaṃ kariṣyati samāhitaḥ ..
vyādhigrastaḥ sa nīrogastatkṣaṇātsaṃbhaviṣyati .. 16 ..
5.211.d:
.. श्रीभगवानुवाच .. ..
अद्य शस्ते दिने योऽत्र सप्तम्यां रविवासरे ..
सूर्योदये नरः स्नानं करिष्यति समाहितः ..
व्याधिग्रस्तः स नीरोगस्तत्क्षणात्संभविष्यति .. 16 ..
5.211.m: The Blessed Lord said: / “Whoever today, on this auspicious day, on a Sunday that is a seventh lunar day, / performs ritual ablution with a concentrated mind at sunrise, / even if afflicted with disease, he shall immediately become free from disease.

5.211.s: nīrogaścepsitānkāmānniṣkāmo mokṣameṣyati .1 17 ..
5.211.d: नीरोगश्चेप्सितान्कामान्निष्कामो मोक्षमेष्यति .1 17 ..
5.211.m: And being free from disease, [if full of desire] he will attain desired desires; if free from desire, he will attain liberation.”

5.211.s:
evamuktvā suraśre ṣṭhoṃ'tardhānaṃ sa gato raviḥ ..
dhanvantariḥ prahṛṣṭātmā svasthānaṃ ca gatastataḥ .. 18 ..
5.211.d:
एवमुक्त्वा सुरश्रे ष्ठोंऽतर्धानं स गतो रविः ..
धन्वन्तरिः प्रहृष्टात्मा स्वस्थानं च गतस्ततः .. 18 ..
5.211.m: Having spoken thus, the Sun, the best of the gods, vanished; / and then Dhanvantari, joyful in mind, went to his own abode.

5.211.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya ratnākṣo'tha mahīpatiḥ ..
ayodhyādhi patiḥ khyātaḥ sūryavaṃśasamudbhavaḥ .. 19 ..
5.211.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य रत्नाक्षोऽथ महीपतिः ..
अयोध्याधि पतिः ख्यातः सूर्यवंशसमुद्भवः .. 19 ..
5.211.m: Now after some time, a king named Ratnākṣa, / the celebrated ruler of Ayodhyā born in the Solar race,

5.211.s:
kṛtajñaśca vadānyaśca svadāranirataḥ sadā ..
śūraḥ paramatejasvī sarvaśatruniṣūdanaḥ .. 6.212.20 ..
5.211.d:
कृतज्ञश्च वदान्यश्च स्वदारनिरतः सदा ..
शूरः परमतेजस्वी सर्वशत्रुनिषूदनः .. 6.212.20 ..
5.211.m: grateful, generous, constantly devoted to his own wife, / brave, supremely splendid, the slayer of all enemies,

5.211.s:
pūrvakarmavipākena tasya bhūmipaterdvijāḥ ..
kuṣṭhavyādhirabhūdraudro duścikitsyo jagattraye ..21..
5.211.d:
पूर्वकर्मविपाकेन तस्य भूमिपतेर्द्विजाः ..
कुष्ठव्याधिरभूद्रौद्रो दुश्चिकित्स्यो जगत्त्रये ..21..
5.211.m: through the ripening of previous karma, O brahmins, / contracted the terrible disease of leprosy, incurable in the three worlds.

5.211.s:
tadasti nauṣadhaṃ loke yattena na kṛtaṃ dvijāḥ ..
kuṣṭhagrastena vā dānaṃ yatra dattaṃ mahātmanā .. 22 ..
5.211.d:
तदस्ति नौषधं लोके यत्तेन न कृतं द्विजाः ..
कुष्ठग्रस्तेन वा दानं यत्र दत्तं महात्मना .. 22 ..
5.211.m: There was no medicine in the world, O brahmins, that was not used by him, / nor any gift that was not given there by that noble-minded man afflicted with leprosy.

5.211.s:
yathāyathauṣadhānyeva sa karoti dadāti ca ..
tathātathā tasya kāyo vyādhinā kṣāmito bhṛśam .. 23 ..
5.211.d:
यथायथौषधान्येव स करोति ददाति च ..
तथातथा तस्य कायो व्याधिना क्षामितो भृशम् .. 23 ..
5.211.m: In whatever manner he took medicines and gave gifts, / in that very manner his body was utterly emaciated by the disease.

5.211.s:
tato vairāgyamāpannaḥ sa nṛpo dvijasattamāḥ ..
putraṃ rājye'tha saṃsthāpya vāṃchayāmāsa pāvakam ..
niṣiddho'pi hi taiḥ sarvaiḥ kalatrairāptasevakaiḥ .. 24 ..
5.211.d:
ततो वैराग्यमापन्नः स नृपो द्विजसत्तमाः ..
पुत्रं राज्येऽथ संस्थाप्य वांछयामास पावकम् ..
निषिद्धोऽपि हि तैः सर्वैः कलत्रैराप्तसेवकैः .. 24 ..
5.211.m: Then, having attained detachment, O best of brahmins, / that king installed his son on the throne and desired to enter the fire, / although he was forbidden by all of them—his wives and trusted servants.

5.211.s:
dattvā dānāni viprebhyaḥ pūjayitvā surottamān ..
saṃbhāṣya ca suhṛdvargaṃ śāsayitvā nijaṃ sutam .. 25 ..
5.211.d:
दत्त्वा दानानि विप्रेभ्यः पूजयित्वा सुरोत्तमान् ..
संभाष्य च सुहृद्वर्गं शासयित्वा निजं सुतम् .. 25 ..
5.211.m: Having given gifts to brahmins, having worshipped the best of gods, / having spoken to the circle of his friends, and having instructed his own son,

5.211.s:
etasminneva kāle tu bhramamāṇe yadṛcchayā ..
kaścitkārpaṭikaḥ prāpto divyarūpavapurdharaḥ .. 26 ..
5.211.d:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु भ्रममाणे यदृच्छया ..
कश्चित्कार्पटिकः प्राप्तो दिव्यरूपवपुर्धरः .. 26 ..
5.211.m: at that very time, while wandering at will, / a certain pilgrim arrived, endowed with a divine form and body.

5.211.s:
athāsau vyākulaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatsarvaṃ nṛpateḥ puram ..
apṛcchadvismayāviṣṭo dṛṣṭvā kañcinnaraṃ dvijāḥ .. 27 .. ..
5.211.d:
अथासौ व्याकुलं दृष्ट्वा तत्सर्वं नृपतेः पुरम् ..
अपृच्छद्विस्मयाविष्टो दृष्ट्वा कञ्चिन्नरं द्विजाः .. 27 .. ..
5.211.m: Then, seeing that whole city of the king agitated, / he, filled with astonishment upon seeing a certain man, asked, O brahmins:

5.211.s:
.. kārpaṭika uvāca .. ..
kimeṣā vyākulā bhadre sarvā jātā mahāpurī ..
nirānandā'śrupūrṇākṣairbālavṛddhairniṣevitā .. 28 ..
5.211.d:
.. कार्पटिक उवाच .. ..
किमेषा व्याकुला भद्रे सर्वा जाता महापुरी ..
निरानन्दाऽश्रुपूर्णाक्षैर्बालवृद्धैर्निषेविता .. 28 ..
5.211.m: The pilgrim said: / “Why has this entire great city become agitated, O good man, / devoid of joy, filled with children and elders whose eyes are full of tears?”

5.211.s:
so'bravīnnṛpatiścāyaṃ kuṣṭhavyādhisamanvitaḥ ..
sādhayiṣyati sandīptaṃ sunirviṇṇo hutāśanam .. 29 ..
5.211.d:
सोऽब्रवीन्नृपतिश्चायं कुष्ठव्याधिसमन्वितः ..
साधयिष्यति सन्दीप्तं सुनिर्विण्णो हुताशनम् .. 29 ..
5.211.m: He said: “This king, afflicted with the disease of leprosy, / deeply despondent, is about to enter the blazing fire.

5.211.s:
teneyaṃ nagarī kṛtsnā paraṃ duḥkhamupāgatā ..
guṇairasya samāviṣṭā nūnaṃ mṛtyuṃ prayāsyati .. 6.212.30 ..
5.211.d:
तेनेयं नगरी कृत्स्ना परं दुःखमुपागता ..
गुणैरस्य समाविष्टा नूनं मृत्युं प्रयास्यति .. 6.212.30 ..
5.211.m: Because of that, this entire city has reached supreme sorrow; / deeply attached to his virtues, it will surely go to death.”

5.211.s: tacchrutvā satvaraṃ gatvā nṛpaṃ kārpaṭiko'bravīt .. 31 ..
5.211.d: तच्छ्रुत्वा सत्वरं गत्वा नृपं कार्पटिकोऽब्रवीत् .. 31 ..
5.211.m: Having heard that, the pilgrim quickly went and spoke to the king,

5.211.s:
sarvaṃ janaṃ narendrasya mṛtaṃ jīvāpayanniva ..
mā nṛpānena duḥkhena vyādhijena hutāśanam ..
praviśa tvaṃ sthite tīrthe sarvavyādhikṣayāvahe .. 32 ..
5.211.d:
सर्वं जनं नरेन्द्रस्य मृतं जीवापयन्निव ..
मा नृपानेन दुःखेन व्याधिजेन हुताशनम् ..
प्रविश त्वं स्थिते तीर्थे सर्वव्याधिक्षयावहे .. 32 ..
5.211.m: as if reviving all the dead people of the lord of men: / “O king, because of this sorrow born of disease, do not / enter the fire, when there exists a sacred ford that brings about the destruction of all diseases!

5.211.s:
madīyo bhūpate deha īdṛgāsīdyathā tava ..
tatra snātasya sadyo'tha jāta īdṛkpunaḥ prabho .. 33 ..
5.211.d:
मदीयो भूपते देह ईदृगासीद्यथा तव ..
तत्र स्नातस्य सद्योऽथ जात ईदृक्पुनः प्रभो .. 33 ..
5.211.m: O king, my body was like yours; / having bathed there, it immediately became like this again, O lord!

5.211.s:
saptamyāṃ sūryavāreṇa bhāskarasyodayaṃ prati ..
yastatra kurute snānaṃ vyādhigrasto naro bhuvi ..34..
5.211.d:
सप्तम्यां सूर्यवारेण भास्करस्योदयं प्रति ..
यस्तत्र कुरुते स्नानं व्याधिग्रस्तो नरो भुवि ..34..
5.211.m: Whoever performs ritual ablution there on a Sunday that is a seventh lunar day / at the rising of the Sun, though afflicted with disease on earth,

5.211.s:
sa vyādhinā vini rmuktastatkṣaṇātkalpatāṃ vrajet..
tathā pāpavinirmukto yathāhaṃ nṛpasattama ..35..
5.211.d:
स व्याधिना विनि र्मुक्तस्तत्क्षणात्कल्पतां व्रजेत्..
तथा पापविनिर्मुक्तो यथाहं नृपसत्तम ..35..
5.211.m: he, freed from disease, would instantly become whole; / likewise he is freed from sins, just as I am, O best of kings.”

5.211.s:
.. rājovāca .. ..
kasmindeśe mahātīrthaṃ tādṛśaṃ vada me drutam .. .. 36 ..
5.211.d:
.. राजोवाच .. ..
कस्मिन्देशे महातीर्थं तादृशं वद मे द्रुतम् .. .. 36 ..
5.211.m: The king said: / “In which country is such a great sacred ford? Tell me quickly!”

5.211.s:
.. kārpaṭikauvāca .. ..
asti bhūmitale khyātaṃ nāgaraṃ kṣetramuttamam ..
kuṣṭhavyādhisamākrāṃto gato'haṃ tatra bhūpate .. 37 ..
5.211.d:
.. कार्पटिकौवाच .. ..
अस्ति भूमितले ख्यातं नागरं क्षेत्रमुत्तमम् ..
कुष्ठव्याधिसमाक्रांतो गतोऽहं तत्र भूपते .. 37 ..
5.211.m: The pilgrim said: / “On the surface of the earth there is the famous, excellent Nāgara sacred field. / Overcome by the disease of leprosy, I went there, O king,

5.211.s:
tasya sandarśanārthāya tīrthayātrāparāyaṇaḥ ..
tatra māṃ dīnamālokya vyādhigrastaṃ suduḥkhitam..
kaścittatrāśrayaḥ prāha tapasvī kṛpayānvitaḥ .. 38 ..
5.211.d:
तस्य सन्दर्शनार्थाय तीर्थयात्रापरायणः ..
तत्र मां दीनमालोक्य व्याधिग्रस्तं सुदुःखितम्..
कश्चित्तत्राश्रयः प्राह तपस्वी कृपयान्वितः .. 38 ..
5.211.m: in order to see it, being intent on a pilgrimage to sacred fords. / Seeing me there, wretched, afflicted by disease, and deeply sorrowful, / an ascetic who was a resident there said out of compassion:

5.211.s:
paścimottaradigbhāge devasya jalaśāyinaḥ ..
tīrthamasti mahāpuṇyaṃ viśvāmitrajalāvaham..39..
5.211.d:
पश्चिमोत्तरदिग्भागे देवस्य जलशायिनः ..
तीर्थमस्ति महापुण्यं विश्वामित्रजलावहम्..39..
5.211.m: ‘In the northwestern quarter from the god who reclines on the waters, / there is a greatly sacred ford bearing the waters of Viśvāmitra.

5.211.s:
tatra gatvā kuru snānaṃ saptamyāṃ ravivāsare ..
māghamāse tu saṃprāpte śuklapakṣe viśeṣataḥ .. 6.212.40 ..
5.211.d:
तत्र गत्वा कुरु स्नानं सप्तम्यां रविवासरे ..
माघमासे तु संप्राप्ते शुक्लपक्षे विशेषतः .. 6.212.40 ..
5.211.m: Having gone there, perform ritual ablution on a Sunday that is a seventh lunar day, / especially when the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha has arrived,

5.211.s:
yena niryāti te kuṣṭho bhāskarasyodayaṃ prati ..
tacchrutvā'haṃ ca tatprāptaḥ saptamyāṃ sūryasaṃyuji ..
tataśca kṛtavānsnānaṃ nirjhare tatra śāṃbhave ..41..
5.211.d:
येन निर्याति ते कुष्ठो भास्करस्योदयं प्रति ..
तच्छ्रुत्वाऽहं च तत्प्राप्तः सप्तम्यां सूर्यसंयुजि ..
ततश्च कृतवान्स्नानं निर्झरे तत्र शांभवे ..41..
5.211.m: whereby your leprosy will depart at the rising of the Sun.’ / Having heard that, I also reached that [place] on a seventh lunar day connected with a Sunday, / and then performed ritual ablution there in the cascade sacred to Śambhu.

5.211.s:
tatastasmādviniṣkrāṃto yāvatpaśyāmyahaṃ tanum..
tāvannṛpedṛśī jātā satyametattavoditam ..42..
5.211.d:
ततस्तस्माद्विनिष्क्रांतो यावत्पश्याम्यहं तनुम्..
तावन्नृपेदृशी जाता सत्यमेतत्तवोदितम् ..42..
5.211.m: Then, having emerged from it, as soon as I looked at my body, / so soon it became like this, O king; this which is told to you is true.

5.211.s:
tasmāttvamapi rājeṃdra tatra snānaṃ samācara ..
saptamyāṃ sūryavāreṇa bhāskarasyodayaṃ prati ..43..
5.211.d:
तस्मात्त्वमपि राजेंद्र तत्र स्नानं समाचर ..
सप्तम्यां सूर्यवारेण भास्करस्योदयं प्रति ..43..
5.211.m: Therefore, O king of kings, you too perform ritual ablution there / on a Sunday that is a seventh lunar day at the rising of the Sun,

5.211.s:
yena te naśyati vyādhirviśeṣamapi pātakam ..
tacchrutvā sa nṛpastūrṇaṃ tenaiva sahito yayau .. 44 ..
5.211.d:
येन ते नश्यति व्याधिर्विशेषमपि पातकम् ..
तच्छ्रुत्वा स नृपस्तूर्णं तेनैव सहितो ययौ .. 44 ..
5.211.m: whereby your disease will be destroyed, and even your great sin.” / Having heard that, the king quickly went along with him.

5.211.s:
cakāra sa tathā snānaṃ saptamyāṃ sūryavāsare ..
māghamāse tu saṃprāpte viśvāmitrajale śubhe .. 45 ..
5.211.d:
चकार स तथा स्नानं सप्तम्यां सूर्यवासरे ..
माघमासे तु संप्राप्ते विश्वामित्रजले शुभे .. 45 ..
5.211.m: He performed ritual ablution thus on a Sunday that is a seventh lunar day, / when the month of Māgha had arrived, in the auspicious water of Viśvāmitra.

5.211.s:
tataḥ kuṣṭhavinirmuktastatkṣaṇātsamapadyata ..
divyarūpavapurddhārī kāmadeva ivāparaḥ .. 46 ..
5.211.d:
ततः कुष्ठविनिर्मुक्तस्तत्क्षणात्समपद्यत ..
दिव्यरूपवपुर्द्धारी कामदेव इवापरः .. 46 ..
5.211.m: Then he immediately became freed from leprosy, / possessing a divine form and body, like a second Kāmadeva.

5.211.s:
atha tuṣṭo nareṃdrastu tasmai kārpaṭikāya ca ..
dadau koṭitrayaṃ hemnaḥ provāca sa tato vacaḥ .. 47..
5.211.d:
अथ तुष्टो नरेंद्रस्तु तस्मै कार्पटिकाय च ..
ददौ कोटित्रयं हेम्नः प्रोवाच स ततो वचः .. 47..
5.211.m: Then the delighted lord of men gave to that pilgrim / thirty million pieces of gold, and then he spoke these words:

5.211.s:
tvatprasādādvimukto'smi rogādasmātsudāruṇāt ..
tasmāttvaṃ gaccha gehaṃ svaṃ sthāsye'haṃ cātra nirbharam .. 48 ..
5.211.d:
त्वत्प्रसादाद्विमुक्तोऽस्मि रोगादस्मात्सुदारुणात् ..
तस्मात्त्वं गच्छ गेहं स्वं स्थास्येऽहं चात्र निर्भरम् .. 48 ..
5.211.m: “By your grace I am freed from this very terrible disease; / therefore, you go to your own home, and I will stay right here with complete peace of mind.

5.211.s:
kariṣyāmi tapo nityaṃ svakalatrasama nvitaḥ ..
rājye saṃsthāpitaḥ putraḥ samartho rājyakarmaṇi .. 49 ..
5.211.d:
करिष्यामि तपो नित्यं स्वकलत्रसम न्वितः ..
राज्ये संस्थापितः पुत्रः समर्थो राज्यकर्मणि .. 49 ..
5.211.m: I will constantly perform austerity together with my wife; / my son, capable in the duties of kingship, has been installed on the throne.”

5.211.s:
ityuktvā prerayāmāsa taṃ tathānyānsamāgatān ..
sevakāsvagṛhāyaiva svayaṃ tatraiva saṃsthitaḥ .. 6.212.50 ..
5.211.d:
इत्युक्त्वा प्रेरयामास तं तथान्यान्समागतान् ..
सेवकास्वगृहायैव स्वयं तत्रैव संस्थितः .. 6.212.50 ..
5.211.m: Having spoken thus, he sent him and the other servants who had come / back to their own homes, while he himself remained right there.

5.211.s:
kṛtvā''śramapadaṃ ramyaṃ svakalatrasamanvitaḥ ..
saṃprāptaśca parāṃ siddhiṃ kālena dvijasattamāḥ .. 51 ..
5.211.d:
कृत्वा'ऽश्रमपदं रम्यं स्वकलत्रसमन्वितः ..
संप्राप्तश्च परां सिद्धिं कालेन द्विजसत्तमाः .. 51 ..
5.211.m: Having made a delightful hermitage together with his wife, / he attained supreme perfection in time, O best of the twice-born. (51)

5.211.s:
tasya nāmnā tataḥ khyātaṃ tīrtha metattriviṣṭape ..
sarvavyādhiharaṃ ramyaṃ sarvapātakanāśanam ..52..
5.211.d:
तस्य नाम्ना ततः ख्यातं तीर्थ मेतत्त्रिविष्टपे ..
सर्वव्याधिहरं रम्यं सर्वपातकनाशनम् ..52..
5.211.m: From his name, this sacred ford then became famed in heaven, / removing all diseases, delightful, and destroying all heinous sins. (52)

5.211.s:
tena saṃsthāpitastatra devadevo divākaraḥ ..
ratnāditya iti khyāto nijanāmnā mahā tmanā .. 53 ..
5.211.d:
तेन संस्थापितस्तत्र देवदेवो दिवाकरः ..
रत्नादित्य इति ख्यातो निजनाम्ना महा त्मना .. 53 ..
5.211.m: There the god of gods, the Sun, was installed by that great-souled one / under his own name, known as Ratnāditya. (53)

5.211.s:
saptamyāṃ sūryavāreṇa tatra snātvā prapaśyati ..
yastu pāpavinirmuktaḥ sūryalokaṃ sa gacchati .. 54 ..
5.211.d:
सप्तम्यां सूर्यवारेण तत्र स्नात्वा प्रपश्यति ..
यस्तु पापविनिर्मुक्तः सूर्यलोकं स गच्छति .. 54 ..
5.211.m: Whosoever, having bathed there on a Sunday which is a seventh lunar day, beholds [him], / is freed from sin and goes to the realm of the Sun. (54)

5.211.s:
yadanyattatra saṃvṛttaṃ kṣetrajātaṃ dvijo ttamāḥ ..
tadahaṃ kīrtayiṣyāmi śṛṇudhvaṃ susamāhitāḥ .. 55 ..
5.211.d:
यदन्यत्तत्र संवृत्तं क्षेत्रजातं द्विजो त्तमाः ..
तदहं कीर्तयिष्यामि शृणुध्वं सुसमाहिताः .. 55 ..
5.211.m: What else happened there, arisen in that sacred field, O best of the twice-born, / that I shall recount; listen with concentrated minds. (55)

5.211.s:
āsīttatra pumānkaściddeśe grāmyo jarātmakaḥ ..
kuṣṭhī tathāpi nityaṃ sa karoti paśu rakṣaṇam ..56..
5.211.d:
आसीत्तत्र पुमान्कश्चिद्देशे ग्राम्यो जरात्मकः ..
कुष्ठी तथापि नित्यं स करोति पशु रक्षणम् ..56..
